entries.name: SmartMesh
entries.reason: LOSS_NOT_ESTABLISHED: the selected transaction exploits transferProxy's unchecked _value + _feeSmt addition and creates artificial SMT ledger balances, but its receipt and call trace transfer no ETH or external reserve asset. Subsequent onchain activity only sends the artificial SMT to exchange deposit addresses; the attacker address records no onchain sale proceeds. The inherited $140M figure has no asset-flow or valuation provenance and does not establish at least $1,000 of stolen or permanently locked assets.

entries.name: Yearn yUSDT fulcrum misconfiguration
entries.reason: CAUSAL_CONFIGURATION: the constructor stored iUSDC where the yUSDT strategy required iUSDT, the value persisted through the exploit, and the trace followed that address. Constructor-set persistent state can establish the vulnerable combination even when the runtime consumes it as written. Reopened pending a deployment anchor, artifact history, and structured loss review.

entries.name: Rho Markets oracle-feed misconfiguration
entries.reason: CAUSAL_CONFIGURATION: rWBTC was listed without an RTokenConfig, leaving its underlying at the zero address, and transaction 0x9d2388a0c449c6265b968d86f0f54e75a5b82e2b04176e35eefdff5f135547ec then assigned the WBTC/USD feed to the zero-address key already used by native ETH. The reviewed incident anchors the resulting ETH price change, complete proxy history, seven-transaction campaign, and 1,233.956023308315527280 wstETH victim outflow.

entries.name: SummerFi impaired-Ark offboarding exposure
entries.reason: CAUSAL_CONFIGURATION: impaired Silo Varlamore Arks had deposit caps set to zero but remained active, so their stale reported value still counted in FleetCommander NAV. The later donation and redemption exercised that persistent offboarding state. Reopened pending the exact state-changing transaction, before/after active-set evidence, artifact history, and structured loss review.

entries.name: VOW temporary usdRate configuration exposure

The reviewed incident reproduces that state 24 seconds before the exploit, the manager execution and mint, and a $1,058,620.25 onchain ETH-and-USDT loss floor.

entries.name: The Sandbox SAND BNB Chain OFT delegate takeover
entries.reason: LOSS_NOT_ESTABLISHED: transaction 0x7ca710d5f575276e12ed7a3617a65002159c87d512fb19e6f59bc31b46b19c95 successfully executes the same OFTSand approveAndCall confused-deputy defect on BNB Chain and changes the LayerZero delegate, but unbacked SAND minted afterward is not victim depletion. The direct, non-proxy BNB runtime was created in transaction 0xe2e732c54c0100eb201159cf09f6d0d219ec6d83ce1deda9ce59041acb607fb7 at block 40897855:19 on 2024-07-29T13:39:09Z, hashes to 0x460fa6e44db22c54a7e236b8fa05d455dc7783be2ed77e711528eca57c729a0b at deployment and pre-anchor, and was 65,095,389 seconds old at takeover. Receipt-level Ethereum reconciliation attributes the 14,753,431.668978-SAND adapter drain to Base source EID 30184; the only isolated BNB source-EID 30102 releases are 1 SAND each in transactions 0xa4a89826af300e2ec210cce6f666f25b689c659d68d8be9c4646feedab650880 and 0xc3e5902d7417776de10018bf72a34ca0e3c42fa20cd056ecd4e82f05dfb85ecf. No exact BNB liquidity-pool or backing-asset depletion of at least $1,000 has been evidenced. This separate-chain campaign can enter the cohort if non-nominal loss above the threshold is established without duplicating the Base-owned Ethereum drain.

entries.name: Curio Ecosystem CurioDAO DSChief hat takeover
entries.reason: MARKET_GOVERNANCE_CAPTURE: the attacker acquired 2 CGT of pre-transaction voting weight against a sitting hat backed by 1 CGT, and DSChief correctly applied its plurality rule. A zero DSPause delay shortened execution but did not turn the valid majority vote into a contract vulnerability. This is market acquisition of privileged control, not a persistent state defect later exercised. Realised extraction was about 180,000 USD; the nominal 16 million USD mint is not loss.

entries.name: Yearn yDAI v1 Curve 3pool strategy slippage
entries.reason: CAUSAL_CONFIGURATION: transaction 0x49d62533adb1131d476ff0a4f67d5a41ba1e65c2ceeb1de54eb8ad9d4f87bf8e selected StrategyDAI3pool for DAI while its slip value was 100 (1 percent); permissionless earn() then exposed that setting in eleven loss-making Curve round trips. The reviewed incident reproduces the activation and complete state history and measures 11,072,464.488546969286678676 DAI of pre-existing depositor loss onchain.

entries.name: Makina Finance DUSD Caliber accounting instruction
entries.reason: CAUSAL_CONFIGURATION: Caliber accepted the vulnerable Curve valuation instruction because it was committed by the timelocked allowedInstrRoot; accountForPosition later verified and executed that approved instruction. Reopened because the root is persistent code-selecting state. Review must still identify its activation transaction and decide whether the 1,299.179984426144193670 WETH depleted from the external Curve DUSD/USDC pool is attributable to this execution context without duplicating another incident.

entries.name: THORChain ETH Router forged Deposit log (second 2021 incident)
entries.reason: OFFCHAIN_ROOT_CAUSE: the loss came from THORChain Bifrost accepting a forged log, not from a defect in the deployed router. Six returnVaultAssets calls in block 12878653 (indices 38,40,42,44,46,48) pass router=0x0 and asgard=attacker contract, so the empty coins loop runs and the unconditional asgard.call{value: msg.value} executes attacker code; that contract then emits the router Deposit topic0 0xef519b7e.. from its own address with topic1 = Asgard vault 0xf56cba49.., carrying each vaults full vaultAllowance read by staticcall in the same block. Bifrost matched logs by topic without checking the emitter and the real Asgard vault then signed legitimate transferOut payouts memoed REFUND:<returnVaultAssets txhash>. The routers own invariants held: vaultAllowance was never mis-decremented and no router asset moved except through the vaults authorised transferOut. THORChains post-mortem locates both bugs and both fixes in Bifrost, and the router runtime 0x8adfb73731c56be8d5d0300c3007489df1f935a40de483e803ef509935950b91 is identical at blocks 12796668, 12828215, 12833113, 12878652 and 13700000, so no redeployment followed. Noted for any future widening of the cohort: returnVaultAssets has no access control and makes an arbitrary external call, which is what let attacker code run inside a router-addressed transaction; that was judged a bypassed precondition rather than an invariant failure of the executed code.

entries.name: THORChain ETH Router phantom deposit (first 2021 incident)
entries.reason: OFFCHAIN_ROOT_CAUSE: Bifrost credited the transactions top-level msg.value instead of the routers truthful Deposit event, which reported amount 0. Wrapper 0x4a33862042d004d3fc45e284e1aafa05b48e3c9c forwards the whole msg.value to attacker EOA 0x3a196410a0f5facd08fd7880a4b8551cd085c031 and then calls Router.deposit{value: 0}(asgard, address(0), amount, SWAP:ETH..); the router correctly emits Deposit(vault, ETH, amount = msg.value = 0, memo). The router paid 2,385.0323146700 ETH across blocks 12833258-12833285 on the strength of the observers misreading. Distinct from the 2021-07-22 incident: different attacker, day and assets. Same router bytecode stability evidence applies.

entries.name: Moonwell cbETH Chainlink OEV feed migration
entries.reason: INCLUDED_CAUSAL_CONFIGURATION: MIP-X43 transaction 0xd26baf29dcba7bf66db4be17b46a49bb4dacca41ace968c98c8a5b09a03ae812 at block 42194663:107 repointed cbETH from USD composite oracle 0xb0ba0c5d7da4ec400c1c3e5ef2485134f89918c5 to raw CBETH/ETH wrapper 0x67996d1ff7a3711a91e2839d1059fcb950c0495d. getUnderlyingPrice(mcbETH) fell from 2,206.683650838065175827e18 to 1.122662744874806300e18. A previously healthy cbETH-backed account was liquidated later in the same block at index 190, so configuration age is 0 seconds. Reaggregating Moonwell's 859-row remediation ledger and excluding its sole $45.997 pre-reset row gives $2,705,352.52 of causal borrower net loss across 858 LiquidateBorrow events.

entries.name: Moonwell mwrsETH anomalous Chainlink round
entries.reason: EXTERNAL_ORACLE_MALFUNCTION: Chainlinks own RSETH/ETH AccessControlledOffchainAggregator 0x4a61db12d0cb4293d799ecdd82e5994b5746f850 (proxy 0xd7221b10fbbc1e1ba95fd0b4d031c15f7f365296, 18 decimals) published one anomalous round: latestAnswer is 1.0559334702744045e18 at block 37722000, 1,649,934,607,316,470,707,093,500 (about 1.56 million times too high, updatedAt 1762235095, 16 s before the exploit) at blocks 37722880-37722882, and 1.056046082284861200e18 again at block 37723500. Moonwells ChainlinkCompositeOracle 0x79c613b4f07080963c3b0ca58eb2745dd4c744a5 multiplied that rate by ETH/USD as designed and returned 5.813066107843462759938890135e27 for mwrsETH, so a dust deposit collateralised millions of borrow. The faulty datum is offchain and no attacker-permitted onchain input produced it, so no defect in executed EVM code caused the loss. Distinct from the 2026-02-15 Moonwell row: different market, mechanism and attacker EOA (0x6997a8c804642ae2de16d7b8ff09565a5d5658ff vs 0x0100ab3021de6e00c39be16424472164c281c308), 103 days apart.

entries.name: Venus Protocol XVS collateral liquidation cascade
entries.reason: MARKET_RISK: Venus used the genuine Chainlink XVS/USD feed and the borrower supplied 1,602,301.549 XVS acquired outside the lending contracts before issuing ordinary borrows. The feed's 83.72 to 140.25 to 87.67 USD sequence was a real market move, with no oracle override. The 80 percent collateral factor changed exposure to that move but did not create a false onchain fact or a later-exercised contract vulnerability.

entries.name: Compound v2 UNI market guarded-price bad debt
entries.reason: CAUSAL_CODE_OR_CONFIGURATION: UniswapAnchoredView 0x50ce56a3239671ab62f185704caedf626352741e rejected a genuine UNI rally outside its 15 percent, 1800-second guard and kept serving 8.34 USD while the reporter reached 10.51 USD. Six transactions borrowed and sold UNI at that stale price, leaving 28,699.96 UNI of bad debt. Reopened because designed behavior does not defeat attribution; review must determine whether the immutable guard is code age or whether a later failover/configuration change reset it, then structure the loss.

entries.name: Moola Market MOO collateral price move
entries.reason: MARKET_RISK: Moola's five-minute sliding-window oracle tracked a sustained MOO market move rather than an attacker-reverted spot distortion. The attacker bought 4.83 million MOO, held it long enough for the TWAP to converge, and did not sell it back; MOO/mCELO remained far above its pre-incident price two days later. The 50 percent LTV and 65 percent liquidation threshold changed lending exposure but did not create a false onchain price or a separate vulnerable state.

entries.name: Kelp DAO rsETH OFTAdapter forged LayerZero packet
entries.reason: CAUSAL_CONFIGURATION_WITH_OFFCHAIN_TRIGGER: EndpointV2 configuration required one DVN, 0x589dedbd617e0cbcb916a9223f4d1300c294236b, and no optional DVN. After that verifier attested a forged nonce-308 packet, permissionless commitVerification and lzReceive released 116,500 rsETH although the Unichain outbound nonce was 307. Reopened because the persistent 1-of-1 verifier set made one compromised service sufficient; review must anchor its activation and separate configuration causality from the offchain trigger.

entries.name: Token of Power Aragon Voting snapshot takeover
entries.reason: MARKET_GOVERNANCE_CAPTURE: Aragon Voting snapshots voting weight, and the attacker bought and held 8,192.000001 of 16,384 TOP before the snapshot, paying 662.855001098310117566 WETH. The 50 percent support rule correctly recognized that pre-transaction majority and granted governance authority. This is market acquisition and exercise of privilege, not a persistent state defect later exercised. True BPool depletion is 281.340475423275038145 WETH; the legacy 1.58 million USD figure includes the attacker's own input.

entries.name: DMM Bitcoin custody theft
entries.reason: NON_EVM_CHAIN: the stolen asset was 4,502.9 BTC out of DMM Bitcoin's Bitcoin hot wallet (theft transaction 975ec405ac9dc9fa5ab8009d94d6a1fe31dff8a8127ea90d023104e52754e4d7, consolidation address 1B6rJRfjTXwEy36SCs5zofGMmdv2kdZw7P, then ten 500-BTC splits). Bitcoin is not an eip155 chain and no EVM contract held, released or accounted for the funds, so no executed EVM code exists to age. The joint FBI, DC3 and Japan NPA advisory of 2024-12-23 attributes the loss to DPRK TraderTraitor operators who social-engineered an employee of Ginco, DMM's wallet-management software vendor, with a fake pre-employment coding test, then used stolen session cookies to impersonate that employee inside Ginco's unencrypted communications system and alter a legitimate DMM withdrawal request in late May 2024. That is an offchain infrastructure and credential failure. EVM chains appear only downstream, when proceeds were bridged through THORChain to Ethereum and Avalanche during laundering, which is not victim depletion.

entries.name: WazirX Safe multisig singleton replacement
entries.reason: SIGNING_PLANE_COMPROMISE: the Safe required four signatures and accepted four threshold-authorized signatures over an execTransaction delegatecall that installed attacker-authored singleton code. WazirX reports that three WazirX and one Liminal signature authorized the malicious transaction. The Safe's authorization checks held, and the later calls used the installed code's privileged drain path; no victim-code or causal-configuration vulnerability was exercised. The 96-second interval ages attack machinery, not battle-tested victim code.

entries.name: Mixin Network cloud database breach
entries.reason: OFFCHAIN_ROOT_CAUSE: Mixin's own disclosure and the SlowMist investigation state that the database of Mixin's cloud service provider was breached, letting the attacker recover the private keys of Mixin's deposit and hot wallet addresses and then sign ordinary transfers. Mixin Kernel is not an eip155 chain, and on the Ethereum side the drained accounts were roughly 11,400 individual per-user deposit externally owned accounts rather than a victim contract, so there is neither a single anchor transaction nor any executed EVM code to age. Reported onchain-confirmed losses are approximately 94.5m USD of ETH and 23.5m USD of DAI on Ethereum plus 23.3m USD of BTC, against the 200m USD headline. Attacker Ethereum addresses reported by SlowMist and BlockSec are 0x52e86988bd07447c596e9b0c7765f8500113104c, 0x3b5fb9d9da3546e9ce6e5aa3cceca14c8d20041e and 0xb5d631a74ad9c9efcf96d6e9e2fabcb75c67eafa; all three show their first activity between 2023-09-22T23:45:35Z and 2023-09-23T01:12:47Z, consistent with the reported window. No victim contract exists.

entries.name: Poloniex hot wallet drain
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: the drained Poloniex wallets are externally owned accounts, not contracts. eth_getCode for the principal drained hot wallet 0xa910f92acdaf488fa6ef02174fb86208ad7722ba returns 0x, so no EVM code executed and none can be aged. The first drain transaction, block 18540957 at 2023-11-10T10:30:11Z, is a plain 4,900 ETH value transfer with empty calldata from that wallet to the Etherscan-labelled attacker 0x0a5984f86200415894821bfefc1c1de036dbf9e7, which forwarded 4,800 ETH onward at 10:41:59Z; roughly 357 further ordinary transfers followed on Ethereum, with separate legs on Tron and Bitcoin. CertiK and Halborn both conclude the hot wallet signing keys were stolen, most plausibly through operator-side malware or social engineering, and Poloniex published nothing contradicting that. Compromised credentials are excluded by METHODOLOGY and no contract sits in the causal path.

entries.name: HTX and HECO Bridge operator key compromise
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: the HECO Bridge access control executed correctly and the attacker simply held the operator keys. The verified non-proxy contract named Bridge at 0xa929022c9107643515f5c777ce9a910f0d1e490c was created at block 11744422 on 2021-01-28T12:54:39Z by 0xd2b75596a63728d84d341f2e3ce6ddae66810128 and held 10,145.844673226576865507 ETH at block 18626539. The anchor transaction at block 18626540 index 6, status 1, is sent by 0x3d655889d197125fb90dcb72e4a287a8410ed1b9 with selector 0xd5b99d3c = withdrawNative(address,uint256,string,bytes32), whose source carries the onlyOperator and whenNotPaused modifiers and requires operatorRequireNum supporting operators. At block 18626539 getOperatorRequireNum() returns 2 and getAdminAddresses('operator') returns exactly [0x3d655889d197125fb90dcb72e4a287a8410ed1b9, 0x6b2286fc3a9265bab3f064808022aca54de4b6ce], so the attacker controlled both authorised operator keys and the 2-of-2 threshold was satisfied as written. The simultaneous HTX hot wallet drains from 0xb9f775179bcc7fcf4534700a48f09c590e390ead, whose eth_getCode is 0x, are ordinary EOA transfers with the same key-management origin. CertiK and SlowMist both conclude operator key compromise; no deployed-code invariant failed, so there is no code-age observation.

entries.name: Nobitex hot wallet destruction
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: Nobitex's EVM-side hot wallets are externally owned accounts. eth_getCode returns 0x for 0xf1beb5ac8da644523974dcd3a907cccac929e817, 0xf22cc3c5b24e3b40ba7a27b82ea0d4b6d3088bbd and 0x293f522e26a3036325e64169f3a90c489ab98484, and the anchor transaction at block 22729002 is a plain ERC-20 transfer (0xa9059cbb) of 939,556.49334 USDT to the unspendable vanity address 0xffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffdead, followed by SHIB, OM, SUSHI and PEPE transfers to the same burn address from 04:36:47Z onward. The campaign also covers Bitcoin, Tron, Dogecoin, Solana, XRP and TON, none of which are eip155 chains. Elliptic and Halborn attribute the loss to hot wallet private keys held on systems the attackers had compromised, and TRM Labs' review of the leaked Nobitex source found master encryption keys in environment variables and plaintext credentials in non-production environments. No contract was called beyond the token contracts themselves, which behaved correctly, so there is no defective EVM code to age.

entries.name: Munchables LockManager rogue-developer proxy drain
entries.reason: PRIVILEGED_ACTION: the deployed code did exactly what its author intended, so there is no defect to age. The LockManager TransparentUpgradeableProxy 0x29958e8e4d8a9899cf1a0aba5883dbc7699a5e1f was created at block 1127735 on 2024-03-21T23:54:45Z by 0xc207fa4b17ca710ba53f06feff56ca9d315915b7 with initial implementation 0x910ffc04a3006007a453e5dd325babe1e1fc4511, whose constructor-time initialize delegatecall wrote the rogue developer's fabricated locked-ETH balance into proxy storage; four minutes later, at block 1127852 on 2024-03-21T23:58:39Z, ProxyAdmin 0x87684be62a2769bbee7b9945ba91d67b53dad153 upgraded to 0xf563ce437e3ab8e0b79585df5122700fbc42afcd, so the backdoor left the live code while the storage entry survived. Both pre-recovery implementations are unverified bytecode. The anchor transaction at block 1339479 is sent by 0x6e8836f050a315611208a5cd7e228701563d09c5 with selector 0x7eee288d and status 1; the LockManager event carries 0x3b0033de4e2bd540000 = 17,413.96 ETH. The actor held the deployer and ProxyAdmin keys, i.e. this is a malicious privileged upgrade by an insider, which METHODOLOGY excludes; ZachXBT and CertiK identify a DPRK-linked contracted developer. 16,311.649 ETH was returned to 0x4d2f75f1cf76c8689b4fddcf4744a22943c6048c on 2024-03-27T05:37:11Z and a Recover implementation 0x55a43849c7f6d1c0bf2ecaf1c3f27ea49880a9a2 was installed at block 1354658.

entries.name: Alphapo payment-processor hot wallet drain
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: the drained Alphapo wallet is an externally owned account. eth_getCode for 0x6dfc34609a05bc22319fa4cce1d1e2929548c0d7 (Etherscan label AlphaPo 1, alphapo.eth) returns 0x, and the anchor transaction at block 17745701 is a plain USDT transfer (0xa9059cbb) to attacker 0x040a96659fd7118259ebcd547771f6ecb9580d17. Roughly 10.7m USD moved on Ethereum against 37.1m USD on Bitcoin and 12.1m USD on Tron, neither of which is an eip155 chain. ZachXBT, Match Systems and Blockchain Intelligence Group all attribute the loss to compromised hot wallet keys (Lazarus), Alphapo published no post-mortem, and no contract other than the correctly functioning token contracts was in the path. Compromised credentials are excluded by METHODOLOGY.

entries.name: BitForex hot wallet extraction
entries.reason: INSIDER_RUG: there is no victim contract and no executed EVM defect. eth_getCode for the BitForex hot wallet 0x3a723e58c4808dde4591543282adc7d6b378715b returns 0x, and the earliest campaign transaction, block 19274789 at 2024-02-21T08:16:23Z, is a deliberate 0.01 ETH test transfer with empty calldata from that wallet to the single destination 0xdcacd7eb6692b816b6957f8898c1c4b63d1fc01f. That destination then received a 10.21 USDT probe at 2024-02-23T19:12:59Z, 40,761 USDT at 22:11:35Z, 258,700 USDC at 2024-02-24T00:09:47Z and further TRB legs, fed by sibling BitForex wallets 0xeec0ed9e41c209c1c53a35900a06bf5dca927405, 0x3c48f8457dbfbcea63aaf936a71d24de7d37cc99, 0x50cbc6faeee68fb63e0a3c8ac8cda8a8505c960b and 0x6cc5f688a315f3dc28a7781717a9a798a59fda7b, alongside Tron and Bitcoin legs. The 58-hour gap between the test and the bulk extraction, the CEO's resignation on 2024-01-31, the unannounced withdrawal halt and the site going dark lead ZachXBT, Decrypt and Halborn to read this as controlled insider extraction rather than an intrusion. BitForex never published a statement, so an operator key theft cannot be formally ruled out, but insider action and compromised credentials are both excluded by METHODOLOGY and neither yields a code-age observation.

entries.name: BtcTurk first custodial-wallet incident
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: the largest evidenced leg is 1,968,794.993 AVAX moved from the attacker consolidation account 0x327a81d0d128db8886d265be73c9fdda97194f30 on Avalanche C-Chain to 0x673f5704020459c8762e3d8e0eb8dac99b9775ba in exactly four plain value transfers with empty calldata between 2024-06-22T02:13:55Z and 06:11:43Z (blocks 47020316, 47020485, 47020548, 47027376). eth_getCode for that account returns 0x and it has no incoming C-Chain or internal transactions, meaning the AVAX arrived through an Avalanche X-Chain to C-Chain atomic import, so the actual victim wallet sits on the non-eip155 X-Chain. BtcTurk's own statement says the attack caused uncontrolled withdrawals from the hot wallets of ten cryptocurrencies while cold storage was untouched, and Halborn concludes a leaked private key. No contract was called and no BtcTurk Ethereum-side victim address is documented by any reputable source, so no code-age observation is possible.

entries.name: CoinEx hot wallet private key leak
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: CoinEx's own announcement names the leakage of the hot wallet private key as the cause. The drained Ethereum wallets are externally owned accounts: eth_getCode returns 0x for 0x33ddd548fe3a082d753e5fe721a26e1ab43e3598 and 0x53eb3ea47643e87e8f25dd997a37b3b5260e7336. The anchor transaction at block 18120510 is a plain 4,946.582 ETH value transfer with empty calldata from 0x33ddd548fe3a082d753e5fe721a26e1ab43e3598 to attacker 0x8bf8cd7f001d0584f98f53a3d82ed0ba498cc3de, which began swapping through routers roughly two hours later. The campaign spans Ethereum, BSC, Polygon and Arbitrum plus non-eip155 Bitcoin, Tron, Solana, XRP, Stellar, Kadena and Bitcoin Cash. SlowMist and Elliptic attribute it to Lazarus and link the infrastructure to the Stake.com and Alphapo incidents. No contract other than correctly functioning token contracts is in the path.

entries.name: BtcTurk second custodial-wallet incident
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: the drained wallets are externally owned accounts and the drain is a scripted sequence of signed transfers, not a contract exploit. eth_getCode returns 0x for 0xb5a46bc8b76fd2825aeb43db9c9e89e89158ecde, 0xde2faca4bbc0aca08ff04d387c39b6f6325bf82a and 0x2cea0297bfb1b55ff37126b677d78e2b1fd2e856. The anchor transaction at block 23138830 is a plain 345.95065004784965 ETH value transfer with empty calldata from 0xb5a46bc8b76fd2825aeb43db9c9e89e89158ecde to the attacker consolidation account 0x7d91d1ebeba91257733a523409125aedac5d8b6e, followed by ERC-20 transfers of FLOKI, PAXG, PEPE, ENA, AAVE, OM and LINK at roughly 12-second intervals across Ethereum, Avalanche, Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, Mantle and Polygon, plus non-eip155 Bitcoin and Solana legs. Rekt and Halborn both conclude leaked hot wallet private keys, the same failure mode as BtcTurk's June 2024 incident; BtcTurk published no post-mortem. Distinct from the 2024-06-22 BtcTurk row: different chains, different wallets and a different attacker cluster.

entries.name: Infini retained deployer admin drain
entries.reason: DIRECT_PRIVILEGED_DRAIN: Infini's deployer retained DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE from contract creation. After 115 days the same authorized account granted itself the withdrawal role and immediately used role-gated calls to redeem and forward 49,516,662.977099 USDC. No intermediate state change created a vulnerability for a later unprivileged transaction; the privileged calls were the drain. Infini states that no key leaked and attributes the loss to failure to revoke the developer's authority.

entries.name: BingX hot wallet compromise
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: the drained BingX wallets are externally owned accounts and the drain is a plain sequence of signed ERC-20 transfers. eth_getCode returns 0x for 0x6c69fa64ec451b1bc5b5fbaa56cf648a281634be and 0xa88f86e5685fca7c5d6de0e4d944875b007137b5. The anchor transaction at block 20787512 moves 32,595.91 USDC from 0x6c69fa64ec451b1bc5b5fbaa56cf648a281634be to attacker 0xf7e8033366166f92eb477b7b38e0d47d47b43326, followed at 12-second intervals by ROG, GMT and dozens of further token legs across Ethereum, BNB Chain, Polygon, Base, Optimism, Arbitrum and Avalanche. BingX CPO Vivien Lin described only abnormal network access to the hot wallet and the exchange published no technical root cause; SlowMist, Elliptic and Cyvers attribute the pattern to Lazarus. Whether the vector was key theft or signing-infrastructure compromise, both are excluded by METHODOLOGY and no contract sits in the causal path, so no code-age observation exists. The headline 2024-09-20 date is Singapore local time.

entries.name: CoinDCX operational wallet server breach
entries.reason: OFFCHAIN_ROOT_CAUSE: the drained wallet is the Solana account Ge8dzF234QHZKFh7TYyZqdipn3BoHyZfoyz9fxEqdTRi, an internal operational account used for liquidity provisioning on a partner exchange; Solana is not an eip155 chain and no EVM contract held the funds. CEO Sumit Gupta describes a sophisticated server breach of that internal account, Merkle Science calls it an infrastructure-level exploit of backend systems managing liquidity operations, and Blockscope describes server-level access enabling unauthorised signing. Customer cold storage was untouched and the loss was absorbed from treasury. EVM chains appear only as attacker plumbing: Ethereum funder EOA 0x23d872d2c091438085253787a5c60dc22e6c8c88 spent its single Tornado-funded output on 2025-07-16T01:56:23Z, and consolidation address 0xef0c5b9e0e9643937d75c229648158584a8cd8d2 received 4,443 ETH on 2025-07-19T08:49:23Z and 7,017 ETH on 2025-07-21T03:11:35Z after the proceeds were bridged back through deBridge and Mayan. Laundering flow is not victim depletion, so there is no EVM victim contract and no code to age.

entries.name: SwissBorg SOL Earn Kiln API supply-chain compromise
entries.reason: NON_EVM_CHAIN: the stolen assets were 192,600 SOL held in Solana stake accounts managed for SwissBorg by Kiln; Solana is not an eip155 chain and no EVM contract was in the path. Kiln's incident report states the entry point was a compromised GitHub access token belonging to a Kiln infrastructure engineer, used to trigger CI/CD workflows in Kiln's infrastructure-as-code repository and inject a malicious payload into the Kiln Connect API; the payload targeted API organisations holding more than 150,000 SOL and appended extra instructions to routine stake-deactivation transactions that reassigned the stake accounts' Staker and Withdrawer authorities to attacker wallets. SwissBorg states its own wallet infrastructure was not breached. The instructions ran against Solana's native staking program, which contained no defect and did exactly what the maliciously constructed transaction asked. This is an offchain third-party supply-chain compromise with no EVM victim contract.

entries.name: Stake.com hot wallet drain
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: the drained Stake.com wallets are externally owned accounts. eth_getCode for the Ethereum hot wallet 0x974caa59e49682cda0ad2bbe82983419a2ecc400 returns 0x, and the anchor transaction at block 18063215 is a plain 6,000 ETH value transfer with empty calldata to the fresh staging address 0x3130662aece32f05753d00a7b95c0444150bcd3c, which forwarded 5,900 ETH onward to 0x94f1b9b64e2932f6a2db338f616844400cd58e8a. Parallel legs ran from BNB Chain hot wallet 0xfa500178de024bf43cfa69b7e636a28ab68f2741 (12,000 BNB at 12:55:23Z, transaction 0xcc696992ac198e8fadd91dbacb8292e9ac23584e111e1e6fafa965de6ece97f0, to BscScan-labelled Stake.com Hacker 0x4464e91002c63a623a8a218bd5dd1f041b61ec04) and Polygon hot wallet 0x019d0706d65c4768ec8081ed7ce41f59eef9b86c (3,000,000 MATIC at 13:00:52Z, transaction 0x30dab44e09593c6aae593fe8b8384d07c51a23b5c9307444f1c293eb7c5f4858). The FBI attributes the theft to Lazarus/APT38 and Stake described unauthorised transactions from its service hot wallets; Hacken, Halborn and Merkle Science all conclude stolen hot wallet keys. Only correctly functioning token contracts were called, so no defective EVM code exists to age.

entries.name: CoinsPaid infrastructure compromise
entries.reason: OFFCHAIN_ROOT_CAUSE: CoinsPaid's own post-mortem states that the attackers did not obtain hot wallet private keys but instead gained access that allowed them to create authorised withdrawal requests, which CoinsPaid's own system then perceived as valid and forwarded to the blockchain. The entry vector was a six-month Lazarus social-engineering campaign in which a CoinsPaid employee took a fake job interview and installed a malicious test application that exfiltrated credentials and gave the attackers a foothold in CoinsPaid infrastructure. The theft and laundering path covers Ethereum and Avalanche C-Chain alongside non-eip155 Bitcoin and Tron, but every movement is an ordinary transfer authorised by CoinsPaid's own custody system, so no contract was exploited and no executed EVM code failed an invariant. Neither CoinsPaid, Match Systems, Elliptic nor the press coverage publishes victim wallet addresses or transaction hashes, so no candidate victim can be named; even with them, an offchain authorisation failure yields no code-age observation. Not to be confused with the separate 2024-01-06 CoinsPaid hot wallet incident of about 7.5m USD.

entries.name: PlayDapp PLA minter-role key compromise
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: the token's access control held and the caller genuinely possessed the role. PLA 0x3a4f40631a4f906c2bad353ed06de7a5d3fcb430 is a verified Solidity 0.5.15 ERC20Capped/Pausable token using stock OpenZeppelin MinterRole, created at block 9921528 on 2020-04-22T09:40:15Z by 0x6f53e6f92e85c084e10aaf35d4a44dee6a27892d, with no proxy and no upgrade events. Exactly two MinterAdded events exist over the token's life: the deployer at creation, and 0xd151050d43c28690766f50ce9ea8686c5d243a40 at block 19190923, added by the anchor transaction whose sender is the pre-existing legitimate minter 0x6f53e6f92e85c084e10aaf35d4a44dee6a27892d calling addMinter (0x983b2d56). The onlyMinter guard was satisfied because the caller held the role, so no invariant failed; the same key then called renounceMinter, locking PlayDapp out. The new minter minted 100,000,000 PLA at 13:45:11Z (0xe8be05f6a3360f63b9e78a30b4ba16ea4c7d0b530a8abf99390f1c831851fb7e), 100,000,000 more at 14:31:23Z, and 1,590,000,000 on 2024-02-12T13:01:47Z, for 1.79 billion PLA nominal against roughly 32m USD actually realised. PlayDapp's post-mortem and PeckShield both state a stolen private key; Halborn's looser access-control framing is contradicted by the onchain caller. Note that OpenZeppelin MinterRole lets any minter add further minters, which is a centralisation choice rather than a defect.

entries.name: Fintoch FintochSTO pool exit
entries.reason: INSIDER_RUG: the contract executed its own arithmetic correctly and the extraction was performed by the operators. FintochSTO 0x19a00e359990ec7daf6e9dd9a2fb7664014bb5f7, verified Solidity 0.5.16, was created at block 19461411 on 2022-07-11T16:05:37Z by 0x8a0deffb71a5dc17a779ab25fdc17fdeb249aa63. The anchor transaction at block 28433724 index 0, status 1, calls swapForUSDT(uint256,uint256) (selector 0x6952f221) with amountFTHIn = 20,001e18 and amountOutMin = 100,000 from the fresh EOA 0xec1a3d4ec207161d3b3341ce19542fecd660aa77, which had been funded with 34,341 FTH minutes earlier by the operator address 0xfce4d8fa21eba2f81bbec1f05f73b639d6023a20, and takes 31,666,317.817 BSC-USD out of the pool. _getUSDTOut implements the textbook constant-product formula amountOut = poolUSDT * amountIn / (poolFTH + amountIn) with no rounding or overflow error, so the entire pool came out only because the pool's FTH reserve was negligible next to the operators' off-pool FTH; the reverse leg swapForFTH is onlyOwner, so no third party could ever have restored the reserve. The contract additionally grants its owner mint, burn, poolBurn and recycleToken. ZachXBT, Hacken and Halborn classify Fintoch as a Ponzi exit scam falsely claiming Morgan Stanley backing with an actor as CEO, and an alleged organiser was later arrested in Thailand. Insider extraction through code working as intended yields no code-age observation.

entries.name: BarnBridge CompoundProvider abandoned-governance controller swap
entries.reason: MARKET_GOVERNANCE_CAPTURE: the attacker bought and locked BOND, then completed BarnBridge's snapshot, proposal, vote, queue, and timelock process over 8.76 days with 63,824.171486555048192 of 213,848.80 BOND staked. Governance validly replaced the controller, and CompoundProvider then honored that privileged controller. This is market acquisition and exercise of governance authority, not a vulnerable state created by an unauthorized transition. Receipt-level loss is 777,075.547933 USDC.

entries.name: FTX post-bankruptcy wallet drain
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: every drained FTX wallet is an externally owned account and every movement is a plain signed transfer, so no EVM code was executed that could carry a defect. eth_getCode returns 0x for the collector 0x59abf3837fa962d6853b4cc0a19513aa031fd32b and for both source wallets. The earliest Ethereum leg is block 15950923 index 56, 2022-11-12T02:22:23Z, transaction 0x6580bf69c1ee28a1d8a4dec9b949272a449b1c58d91e6692ef34d9ea40fd9653: 9,500 ETH with empty calldata from the FTX hot wallet 0x2faf487a4414fe77e2327f0bf4ae2a264a776ad2, followed at block 15950963 by 10,000 ETH from the second FTX wallet 0x7abe0ce388281d2acf297cb089caef3819b13448 (0x9c9065a994e2c9dfb2...). The collector then approved and swapped through DEX routers, which is laundering rather than victim depletion. Elliptic put the unauthorised transfers at about 477m USD across Ethereum, BSC, Solana and others in the hours after the Chapter 11 filing. In January 2024 a federal grand jury in Washington DC indicted Robert Powell, Carter Rohn and Emily Hernandez for a SIM-swap conspiracy that defeated the multifactor authentication on the victim company's accounts; that is an offchain credential failure, and DefiLlama's hacks dataset likewise files the incident under social engineering/phishing. No contract invariant failed anywhere in the path.

entries.name: Wormhole token bridge forged VAA
entries.reason: NON_EVM_CHAIN: the defect is in Wormhole's Solana core-bridge program, written in Rust, not in any eip155 contract. verify_signatures used the deprecated solana_program::sysvar::instructions::load_current_index, which reads the supplied account without checking that it is the real Instructions sysvar; the attacker passed a fabricated account that made the secp256k1 precompile check appear satisfied, posted a VAA with no valid guardian signatures, and called complete_wrapped to mint 120,000 whETH on Solana. The Ethereum side then behaved exactly as designed: the guardians observed the (fraudulent but on-chain) Solana burn and signed genuine VAAs, so the token bridge 0x3ee18b2214aff97000d974cf647e7c347e8fa585 released 93,750 ETH to 0x629e7da20197a5429d30da36e77d06cdf796b71a in three internal transfers - 10,000 ETH at 2022-02-02T18:26:03Z (0x4d5201dd4a377f20e61fb8f42e6f929ec16bcec918f0584e39241d15b254a80f), 3,750 ETH at 18:33:32Z (0xd31b155e259a403ebe69831fae0ec2b4bd33dfa090c43b605a57d5c72c4fbbc7) and 80,000 WETH at 18:28:37Z via completeTransferAndUnwrapETH, selector 0xc6878519, transaction 0x24c7d855a0a931561e412d809e2596c3fd861cc7385566fd1cb528f9e93e5f14, unwrapped at 18:48:48Z. Because the EVM contract's signature check passed on genuinely signed data, there is no defective EVM code to age.

entries.name: Drift Protocol admin takeover and fake-collateral drain
entries.reason: NON_EVM_CHAIN: Drift is a Solana perpetuals protocol and every contract in the path is an SVM program, so no eip155 code exists to age. The attack was also not a code defect: per Chainalysis, Elliptic and TRM Labs the operators abused Solana durable nonces to get Drift Security Council members to sign transactions out of band that later executed and handed over protocol admin authority, then used that authority to whitelist a worthless attacker-created SPL token (CVT) as collateral at an attacker-set price, deposited 500,000,000 CVT and withdrew about 285m USD of USDC, SOL and ETH. Both halves - social engineering of privileged signers and an admin parameter change - are exclusion grounds independent of the chain. DefiLlama records the incident as Solana, 295m USD, access control / proxy upgrade hijack. Elliptic and TRM attribute it to DPRK-linked operators.

entries.name: KuCoin hot wallet drain
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: the drained KuCoin wallets are externally owned accounts - eth_getCode returns 0x for the attacker 0xeb31973e0febf3e3d7058234a5ebbae1ab4b8c23 and for all three source wallets 0x689c56aef474df92d44a1b70850f808488f9769c, 0x2b5634c42055806a59e9107ed44d43c426e58258 and 0x6e9c171a95ed3b67bd299135f70c967d1231e24c. The earliest Ethereum leg is block 10933499 index 16, 2020-09-25T18:48:59Z, transaction 0x02bcb11691a2ce8f1e8ca4f3f943bdea2308a89308ca42bc67dea4bcb5de1413: 1,994.2095 ETH with empty calldata; 8,709.03 ETH followed 19 seconds later from the second wallet, and block 10933501 carries the bulk ERC20 sweep (13,888,191.45 USDT, 3,459,405.23 ORN, 475,856,068.74 KAI and dozens more), all ordinary transfer calls that the token contracts executed correctly. KuCoin's own disclosure and Chainalysis both state that the hot wallet private keys were obtained; Chainalysis attributes the theft to Lazarus. The stolen set spans Bitcoin, BSV, LTC, XLM, XRP and EOS/Omni USDT alongside Ethereum, and about 84 percent was later recovered through tracking, contract upgrades by affected token issuers and judicial action - none of which changes that no executed EVM code failed an invariant.

entries.name: BitMart hot wallet drain
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: BitMart's Ethereum and BNB Chain hot wallets are externally owned accounts and the theft is a long run of ordinary ERC20 and BEP20 transfer calls. eth_getCode for the BitMart hot wallet 0x68b22215ff74e3606bd5e6c1de8c2d68180c85f7 at block 13742126, the block before the first drain, is 0x (it carries an EIP-7702 delegation designator today, which post-dates the incident by years), and the collector 0x39fb0dcd13945b835d47410ae0de7181d3edf270 is likewise an EOA. The earliest leg is block 13742127, 2021-12-04T21:31:09Z, transaction 0x6afb730976b2cf39e5ea7ce8a56c3597728e4e5923f7abae7086fb53019e81e8, moving 893,755,205,648.56 SHIB; SAITAMA, ELON, GALA and CRO follow within 65 seconds, and the first ETH transfer is 100 ETH at 22:10:46Z (0xcfe595f7e958863cf302adffb02318d7ad2d730b8e7c0c9dd6901054f56eaa5b). Proceeds were swapped through 1inch (selector 0x7c025200) and sent to Tornado Cash, and 18,085 ETH was later consolidated into 0x4bb7d80282f5e0616705d7f832acfc59f89f7091. BitMart CEO Sheldon Xia stated publicly that a stolen private key was the cause; CertiK reached the same conclusion. No contract was exploited.

entries.name: Vulcan Forged Venly custodial wallet key compromise
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: the victims are 96 individual user wallets whose private keys were held by Vulcan Forged's integrated custodial wallet provider Venly, not any contract. On Polygon the attacker 0x48ad05a3b73c9e7fac5918857687d6a11d2c73b1 received exactly 96 inbound PYR transfers from 96 distinct sender addresses totalling 4,936,266.221034305 PYR (token 0x348e62131fce2f4e0d5ead3fe1719bc039b380a9) between block 22452791 at 2021-12-12T22:29:45Z (transaction 0x4d3433f5f6620bbfde37b9ffa63621443a2e30cc2b6628713c104371ed8f2761, 116,133.59 PYR from 0xf8ae7b099c0140d51e955723824f5ec3665edde0) and block 22457371 at 2021-12-13T01:13:37Z - a sender count that matches Vulcan Forged's own statement about 96 compromised addresses. The same EOA collected assets on Ethereum from 22:27:32Z. Every movement is a plain ERC20 transfer signed by the legitimate key holder of record, so the token contracts executed correctly. Corroborating onchain fact: the PYR ERC20 that now sits at 0x430ef9263e76dae63c84292c3409d61c598e9682 on Ethereum was only created at block 13849184 on 2021-12-21T14:57:25Z by 0xab9aab1a5aed928998399dd0c5bb602d968deea5, eight days after the theft - the remedy was a token redeployment and reimbursement, not a contract fix, because there was no defective contract.

entries.name: BXH VaultPool controller admin key drain
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: the funds left through BXH's own pre-existing, correctly gated controller path, driven by a compromised administrator key. The victim is the verified VaultPool 0x6aceca12de5a15f11ca51b654433259533b0b802, created at block 9512275 on 2021-07-27 by the BXH deployer 0x56146b129017940d06d8e235c02285a3d05d6b7c, whose controller() is 0x83dae57c46985c3a2346e8a3c6991ca908f8b06b - deployed by that same BXH deployer at block 9512077 on 2021-07-27T04:07:08Z, three months before the incident, and holding the vault's unlimited ERC20 allowance by design (allowance(vault, controller) for BUSD at block 12209241 is 2^256-1 minus dust). In the anchor at block 12209242 index 79 the attacker EOA 0x48c94305bddfd80c6f4076963866d968cac27d79 calls its own proxy 0x887716168fc8c1a2933f97ea3858a94c9e229201 (which it created at block 12136755) with selector 0x4eea9a8d; the callTracer shows that proxy invoking the genuine controller with selector 0x08b6b802, and the controller issuing transferFrom against the vault for 13,304.601043634097657875 ETH-BEP20, 24,669,898.22 BSC-USD, 6,415,713.63 BUSD, 2,428,246.61 USDC, 15,546.82 WBNB, 642.89 BTCB and 13,999.56 XRP, all forwarded to the attacker through its collector 0x13b81fa9c0873a74c49a85bd8149c1c20bf9d18c. BXH's own statement, reported by CoinDesk, is that the administrator's private key was obtained, most likely through the keyholder's machine or an insider; the controller is unverified on BscScan so its access modifier cannot be read directly, but nothing in the trace shows a bypassed check - the drain used a three-month-old authorised path with a valid caller. No invariant of executed code was violated, so there is no code-age observation.

entries.name: Atomic Wallet client key exfiltration
entries.reason: OFFCHAIN_ROOT_CAUSE: the victims are individual users' externally owned accounts across roughly 13 chains (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tron, BSC, Polkadot, Avalanche, XRP and others) and the keys were obtained off-chain from the Atomic Wallet client or its distribution/update path. A representative Ethereum leg is block 17395844 index 5, 2023-06-02T21:56:23Z, transaction 0x9d6903b106a948d20f6b967a6fa1c2472b73868e00ca2496fc7c1f37d4cc1d86: 304.363031583184322615 ETH with empty calldata from user EOA 0xb02dab4490fec2deaecc336f8b8b5e10dd8c6072 to drainer 0x391628df29ac2b66c11ae9515289a26be06a6340, which has code 0x and exactly one inbound value transfer - one of many single-use collectors. Atomic Wallet never published a root cause; the candidate vectors discussed publicly are a BGP hijack of Atomic Wallet traffic, unremediated findings from Least Authority's 2021 review, and client-side key leakage of the Slope kind. DefiLlama files the incident as a supply-chain attack, and the FBI has attributed it to Lazarus. Whichever vector is correct, no contract was called with malformed input and no EVM code failed an invariant, so no code-age observation exists.

entries.name: Liquid Global hot wallet drain
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: the drained Liquid wallet is an externally owned account. eth_getCode is 0x for both the Liquid hot wallet 0x9cc2dce817093ceea82bb67a4cf43131fa354c06 and the attacker 0x5578840aae68682a9779623fa9e8714802b59946. The earliest Ethereum leg is block 13051251 index 13, 2021-08-18T20:00:41Z, transaction 0xea9fb379835ba06ec6785a595444897d8cb897d511cb43abfa548da30fef3cc7, an ordinary USDT transfer of 3,246,048.448533; 2,063,297.938773 USDC follows at 20:03:50Z (0x9bf1af79864fff64d3f7884aee69c08a78fdb9708ee88f2a6451c68a5f0dc0d7), then 507,311.1724 CEL and a long tail of ERC20s, with parallel legs on Bitcoin, XRP and Tron. Liquid Global's own announcement of 2021-08-19 states that its warm and hot wallets were compromised, and DefiLlama classes it as a hot wallet key compromise of about 91.35m USD. Only correctly functioning token contracts were called, so there is no defective EVM code to age.

entries.name: AscendEX hot wallet drain
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: one private key was reused for the same hot wallet address on three chains and all three were emptied within minutes, which is the signature of a stolen key rather than a contract defect. The AscendEX hot wallet 0x986a2fca9eda0e06fbf7839b89bfc006ee2a23dd has code 0x on Ethereum, BNB Chain and Polygon alike, as does the collector 0x2c6900b24221de2b4a45c8c89482fff96ffb7e55, which holds the identical address on all three. The earliest Ethereum leg is block 13785860, 2021-12-11T19:52:50Z, transaction 0x346e2691db2b3a4931a188372dfeddecfb31e507604a33a6992c99dd0941f6b4, a plain transfer of 693.4196422074118 AXS, followed by 1,767,168.50 FTM, 4,560,610.528488 USDT and 4,566,868.43738 USDC inside four minutes; the Polygon leg starts at 19:52:58Z (192,198.56 ROUTE, 0x40bf0e0c80ca6e2ed3d5958efba532dd1aa7b90450b5e3b153f33de20bd4fdfc) and the BNB Chain leg at 20:13:00Z (0x2c975ef076dcb7c3d8fb2ebc27c0bd8ba6af5dbf3c45ec20624aab4deba72ef8). Rekt's breakdown of 60m USD on Ethereum, 9.2m on BSC and 8.5m on Polygon matches, and AscendEX's own notice describes unauthorised transfers from a compromised hot wallet. No contract invariant failed.

entries.name: EasyFi admin wallet key compromise
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: the drained EasyFi wallets are externally owned accounts, not contracts, and every transfer is an ordinary ERC20 call. On Ethereum the attacker 0x83a2eb63b6cc296529468afa85dbde4a469d8b37 takes 1,799,990 EASY (token 0x913d8adf7ce6986a8cbfee5a54725d9eea4f0729) at block 12269958, 2021-04-19T10:26:19Z, transaction 0x82bca5138041b8c7ad99db3b3c893fbfee2ba175826b827de8c09689b8b513e2, from 0xf59c2e9d4ab5736a1813738e5aa5c3f5eaf94d9e (code 0x), then 1,035,555.83 EASY plus the UNI-V2 LP position from 0x0c08d0fe35515f191fc8f0811cadcfc6b2615b74 (code 0x). On Polygon the same EOA takes 436,014.6 and 447,086.07 EASY from 0xf4ee731c6ebeae783f7a03ec5bfc18489c8a4db9 and 0x50735f9087a148f4ba4a0f0052511c3bc5687d4c, then the treasury EOA 0x6324b1f720a07435269ae84285b1bafa4800fb3e (also code 0x) yields 1,979,435.98 DAI, 2,050,166.555442 USDC.e, 1,854,474.025921 USDT and 139.2994785 WETH between 11:05:29Z and 11:07:11Z. Every inbound sender on both chains that carries protocol funds is an EOA. EasyFi founder Ankitt Gaur's post-mortem states that the machine used solely for official transfers was compromised and the admin key taken; the key was in a MetaMask hot wallet with no multisig and no timelock. DefiLlama files it as social engineering / malware. Nominal EASY at the reported rate produced the 59m-80m USD headline against roughly 6m USD of actually liquid stablecoins and ETH.

entries.name: bZx Polygon and BSC deployer key compromise
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: the contracts' ownership checks all passed because the attacker held the owner key. The victims are the verified bZxProtocol 0xfe4f0eb0a1ad109185c9aade64c48ff8e928e54b (Polygon, created block 14612379, 2021-05-17T17:32:45Z) and LoanToken 0x97ebf27d40d306ad00bb2922e02c58264b295a95 (Polygon, block 14964301, 2021-05-26T20:49:03Z), plus bZxProtocol 0xc47812857a74425e2039b57891a3dfcf51602d5d on BNB Chain, all deployed by the bZx developer EOA 0xb7f72028d9b502dc871c444363a7ac5a52546608. Exactly one OwnershipTransferred event exists on each between deployment and the incident: Polygon bZxProtocol at block 21009330, 2021-11-05T11:07:16Z, anchor transaction 0xbb1452e04d9b3451dd2f08920deadf3009e1e8233289cd628a391bdc1c37555d, moving ownership from 0xb7f72028d9b502dc871c444363a7ac5a52546608 to the fresh EOA 0x0acc0e5faa09cb1976237c3a9af3d3d4b2f35fa5; the LoanToken follows at block 21009382 (0xc078907ec967b68f257b5d809ab71dbbc56288d158861de6b357ed0aea59fd75) and the BNB Chain protocol at block 12386620 (0x9b16f5e8a648f72be3f9657880b26e525018e40e8873a14161690f8f48bf01b9). owner() read at block 21009445 is 0x0acc0e5f..., and that same address then calls selector 0x55072d96 with the collector 0x74487eed1e67f4787e8c0570e8d5d168a05254d4 as argument to sweep 5.88210232 WBTC (block 21009446, 0x028d92aac9e58572d6099973729ebfbdfa405566a5aa2386cad6a0744876f107), then 568.54 WETH, 27.35 WBTC and 283,459.66 WMATIC at 11:15:02Z, and on BNB Chain 651.01 WBNB, 56,162.25 CAKE, 11.91 BTCB and 87.80 ETH at 11:14:07Z. bZx's post-mortem states that a developer opened a phishing email carrying a macro-bearing Word document which ran a script that stole his wallet mnemonic; that EOA controlled the Polygon and BSC deployments. Ethereum was unaffected because it was under DAO control. A compromised owner key is not a defect in executed code.

entries.name: Cashio CASH infinite mint
entries.reason: NON_EVM_CHAIN: Cashio was a Solana stablecoin protocol and the defective program is Rust running on the SVM, so it produces no eip155 code-age observation. The bug was a missing account-constraint chain in the mint instruction: the collateral bank account's `crate_collateral_tokens` was validated against the pool but the pool account itself was not validated against the crate, so an attacker could supply a fake Saber LP mint that chained back to attacker-controlled accounts and mint CASH against worthless collateral. Roughly two billion CASH were minted and drained for about 52.8m USD of UST/USDC LP collateral, and CASH depegged to zero. There is no EVM contract anywhere in the path - Cashio had no Ethereum, BSC or L2 deployment - so no victim contract, exploit transaction or executable code age can be recorded in this cohort. DefiLlama records the incident as Solana, 52.8m USD, missing input validation.

entries.name: Step Finance treasury executive-device compromise
entries.reason: NON_EVM_CHAIN: Step Finance operates only on Solana and both attacker wallets and both theft transactions are Solana artifacts - collector LEP1uHXcWbFEPwQgkeFzdhW2ykgZY6e9Dz8Yro6SdNu and secondary 7raxiejD8hDUH1wyYWFDPrEuHiLUjJ4RiZi2z1u2udNh, the stake-authority/unstaking transaction 5EeXqPQci3ZnbFGWPJf622cLqLGnMuNcAr1rDGCizKRFt9owawCzovNpBC4xNh7A4a5p7Qkvsg8nPaYmw3MiYCvF and the 261,932 SOL withdrawal 4Ly35PsVTBNPVibpDRww6FC43pU5Tuw6UtaKECzcLKXtWTPyyvw1dw8LoNRLBDMgQUP81nN69mhiAEDJvzL8X317. No eip155 contract is in the path. The cause is also an exclusion ground on its own: an executive's device was compromised, most plausibly by social engineering, and the attacker used the resulting legitimate signing authority to reassign stake authorisation and approve withdrawals. No program was exploited and no on-chain invariant failed. DefiLlama records the incident as Solana, private key compromised, about 40m USD; rekt puts the realised figure at 27.3m USD.

entries.name: Scream v3 aliased stablecoin price feeds
entries.reason: CAUSAL_CONFIGURATION: scDEI, scFUSD, scTUSD, scDOLA, and scFRAX returned the same changing value as the USDC feed, showing that distinct stablecoins were aliased to persistent USDC pricing state while DEI traded below par. The largest DEI supply, 10,425,082.84 DEI in transaction 0x2834828184166a609ffe24c496f9047ca37bcdb8a16a8226098debab98c9bce3, preceded later borrows and roughly 35 million USD of bad debt. Reopened pending the original feed-assignment anchor, a coherent exploit anchor, and victim-depletion evidence.

entries.name: Crypto.com 2FA bypass withdrawals
entries.reason: OFFCHAIN_ROOT_CAUSE: the loss came from Crypto.com's own withdrawal system approving unauthorised requests, not from any contract. The onchain fingerprint is unambiguous: the collector 0x6e1218c55f1acb588fc5e55b721f1183d7d29d3d has code 0x and received 282 inbound value transfers from 282 distinct sender addresses totalling 4,836.25962449635 ETH, all inside two hours on 2022-01-17 between block 14024742 at 18:44:35Z (first transaction 0x49121cabf0b68f4755aa766090cbbc4fde4cca79d62365dadc4c92a83c683cda, 8.4207791732 ETH from 0x0c405c16c379b67d256f6883803e68d50dd2f327) and block 14025319 at 20:55:35Z. Many small transfers from many unrelated user accounts to one address is the signature of an exchange approving withdrawals it should not have, which is exactly what Crypto.com's own 2022-01-20 report describes: transactions were approved without the 2FA control being entered, affecting 483 accounts, 4,836.26 ETH, 443.93 BTC and about 66,200 USD in other currencies. DefiLlama files it as session key compromised. Nothing but correctly functioning transfers appears on chain, so there is no defective EVM code to age.

entries.name: Meerkat Finance vault backdoor upgrade
entries.reason: PRIVILEGED_ACTION and INSIDER_RUG: the code that failed was installed by the protocol's own proxy admin four minutes before it was used, so it never aged and was never trusted by anyone but its author. The two victim proxies are the BUSD vault 0x7e0c621ea9f7afd5b86a50b0942eaee68b04a61c and the WBNB vault 0x639f18c72b6a017bdd209c161d1617c9481a1e4d; reading the EIP-1967 slots at block 5381245 gives admin 0xc1f78cc844ac8e2dd9335e70b9c645e4d79130c5, the Meerkat deployer, and implementation 0x49509a31898452529a69a64156ab66167e755dfb, the honest logic that deployer created on 2021-03-03T16:28:07Z. The replacement implementations 0x9d3a4c3acee56dce2392fb75dd274a249aee7d57 and 0xb2603fc47331e3500eaf053bd7a971b57e613d36 were created by 0xfc76e716c35633a93ad621099a52ffda912fbedd at 2021-03-04T08:49:46Z and 08:49:58Z; the deployer key then called upgradeTo (selector 0x3659cfe6) on the WBNB vault at block 5381239, 08:53:10Z (0x063970f8625f250101a7da8abf914748cf8eaaaa9458041f1928501accfe5d6c) and on the BUSD vault at block 5381246, 08:53:31Z (0xf19fa4bcff4adaebeddd28c851458ba0f01ffedd52b62df56ace94e7c8842553). The new logic exposes an unprotected init(address) (0x19ab453c), called 24 seconds later at block 5381254 by 0x9542966f1114eaa5859201aa8d34358bfedbfa79 (0xfcf48681e382e9f9cc1d6a64ff30487306f6b869924c6594075fcc86b3b21f5d) to take ownership and drain. Balances confirm the outcome: the BUSD vault held 13,968,039.801181389726119981 BUSD at block 5381245 and 0 at block 5381300; the WBNB vault held 73,635.237472535387195192 WBNB at block 5381238 and 0 at 5381300. Meerkat first claimed a hack, and DefiLlama classifies it as a rugpull / admin drain. Attacker-authored code installed by the operator's own key yields no code-age observation.

entries.name: Humanity Protocol foundation key and ProxyAdmin compromise
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE and PRIVILEGED_ACTION: the drain ran through an attacker-authored implementation installed by the legitimate ProxyAdmin, twelve seconds before use. The first leg is a plain ERC20 transfer of 6,045,060.xx H (token proxy 0xcf5104d094e3864cfcbda43b82e1cefd26a016eb) from the Humanity hot wallet 0x0fd9c51999ae46a0e1b21a235e0a529bbcc4612a to 0x9e995952ef7665b243eeef0693acd7fed7150504 at block 25274211, 2026-06-08T17:32:23Z (0x94a4b4a37439ad5c01a84b504c7f58eb5c2ab560352f147f78e62802bf4ee015). The bridge TransparentUpgradeableProxy 0x44f161ae29361e332dea039dfa2f404e0bc5b5cc, created 2025-06-20T18:56:35Z with implementation 0xfe1a06260b3b68f49862ae5d617686d78f454dea, then emits exactly one further Upgraded event, to 0xee1bd9356fe66591f600d5769f3e0e03f012cafa at block 25274909, 2026-06-08T19:52:11Z (0xca98624bf0425cba8fa89081be6981e34d7b3023f810350d0a0158de0eb4c551); the very next block carries 0xa665998ca9a2fcfe66d687647edede62c7acd554c7d35ea13c93788b8a129e5b, in which 0xd1ea823d421e0c829ee11f772af487fd352678ea calls execute(address) (0x4b64e492) on that fresh implementation to sweep the escrow. The H token proxy was likewise upgraded to 0xa4dcfaf7a2c0a533bc00a8a6d93b9f25f4583bb7 at 2026-06-09T01:05:11Z and restored to its original implementation 0x761c06a46d3c85ecd87cf6917b3de329b95829be on 2026-06-22. On BNB Chain the same proxy address 0x44f161ae29361e332dea039dfa2f404e0bc5b5cc was made to mint 100,000,000 H per call via mint(address,uint256) (for example 0x5a8f82f1064a7846ab3eb77bd1d36ec52dfd773c3957ad0aeea28da95fe9c5fb). The published account is that a director's laptop was infected through a spear-phishing email impersonating Bithumb, giving the attacker seven production keys backed up a year earlier and never rotated - three of six signers on the Ethereum Safe, three of five on the BSC Safe, and the ProxyAdmin on both chains, which had no timelock. DefiLlama records private key compromise, Ethereum and BSC, about 32m USD. Access control was satisfied throughout, so no executed code failed an invariant.

entries.name: Upbit Solana hot wallet drain (November 2025)
entries.reason: NON_EVM_CHAIN: the assets taken in Upbit's 2025-11-27 incident were Solana-ecosystem tokens held in a Solana hot wallet, so no eip155 contract is in the path and no EVM code age can be measured. DefiLlama's hacks dataset records the incident with chain ['Solana'] alone (36m USD, social engineering / malware), separate from Upbit's earlier 2019-11-27 Ethereum incident which the same dataset lists as ['Ethereum']. The cause is independently an exclusion ground: a custodial hot wallet's signing authority was abused, reported as malware / operator compromise rather than any contract flaw, and Upbit's own notice frames it as unauthorised outbound transfers that it covered from company assets. Distinguish this from the 2019 Upbit Ethereum theft; that is a different candidate and a different chain. This exclusion rests on the chain attribution plus the custodial cause; no victim contract or exploit transaction is named anywhere in the reporting because there is none.

entries.name: Deribit hot wallet drain
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: Deribit's drained wallet is an externally owned account and the theft is a bare value transfer. eth_getCode is 0x for both the Deribit hot wallet 0x8d08aad4b2bac2bb761ac4781cf62468c9ec47b4 and the attacker 0xb0606f433496bf66338b8ad6b6d51fc4d84a44cd. The anchor is block 15878752 index 56, 2022-11-02T00:27:23Z, transaction 0xdd608c8c4e8d8529967955d89f9e71842e80c3c84d592c72054f68090a5a102c: 9,080.186758793618 ETH, empty calldata, from the hot wallet straight to the attacker, with a further 31.404516258391762 ETH at 08:35:23Z (0xf3a14bfddc65725b4a345e0bafa84afd328de1b9487339157a0f24c9085b66f2); Bitcoin legs ran in parallel to bc1qw5g8lw4kzltpdcraehy2dt6dqda8080xd6vhl4kg4wwsypwerg9s3x6pvk. Deribit's own statement of 2022-11-02 describes a hot wallet compromise covered from company reserves, with client funds unaffected and cold storage untouched; DefiLlama records a hot wallet key compromise of about 28m USD. Note that the 'DERIBIT' ERC20 that appears in the attacker's token history at 08:16:11Z the same morning is an unrelated spam token minted from the zero address, not part of the theft. No contract was called and no code failed.

entries.name: GALA v2 dormant minter-role key compromise
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: the anchor transaction is a bare mint(address,uint256) call (selector 0x40c10f19) sent at block 19913232 by externally owned account 0xec78b484a28a73f4f1cff23b9cd31aa12c1d9b4e directly to the GALA v2 token proxy 0xd1d2eb1b1e90b638588728b4130137d262c87cae; status 1, exactly one log, a Transfer from the zero address of raw 500000000100000000 (5,000,000,001 GALA at 8 decimals) to 0xe2ca471124b124831e231fb835778840ad100f97. That EOA was a dormant third party still holding the token's minter role after a 2023 partner integration; Gala's own incident report and rekt.news both describe a compromised minter key. The deployed code did exactly what it says: an authorised minter minted. There is no invariant failure in executed EVM code, so no code-age observation exists. The owner-controlled blocklist froze the recipient and capped realised loss at about 21.8m USD (5,913 ETH, returned two days later) against the roughly 216m USD nominal mint.

entries.name: BigONE production-network supply chain compromise
entries.reason: OFFCHAIN_ROOT_CAUSE: SlowMist's incident alert states that BigONE's production network was breached and the operating logic of the account-management and risk-control servers was modified so that unauthorised withdrawals were signed and broadcast normally, and that no private keys were leaked. The named Ethereum sink is 0x9bf7a4ddca405929dba1fbb136f764f5892a8a7a; onchain it is an externally owned account (code size 0) whose earliest inbound transfers begin 2025-07-15T17:25:59Z and come from BigONE hot-wallet EOA 0xd4dcd2459bb78d7a645aa7e196857d421b10d93f (also code size 0): USDT 1,395,000 (tx 0x605e999e7be320c893...), INVI 4,702,000, XIN 20,730, CDT 1,901,300 and UNI 25,487 in the following minutes. The same actor holds BSC 0x9bf7a4ddca405929dba1fbb136f764f5892a8a7a, Solana HSr1FNv266zCnVtUdZhfYrhgWx1a4LNEpMPDymQzPg4R, Bitcoin bc1qwxm53zya6cuflxhcxy84t4c4wrmgrwqzd07jxm and Tron TKKGH8bwmEEvyp3QkzDCbK61EwCHXdo17c. Every EVM leg is a plain ERC-20 transfer between two EOAs: there is no victim contract and no defective executed code, only compromised offchain infrastructure.

entries.name: FixedFloat custodial wallet drain (first 2024 incident)
entries.reason: OFFCHAIN_ROOT_CAUSE: FixedFloat is a custodial instant-exchange service, not a protocol. About 26.1m USD of Bitcoin and Ethereum was taken from its own service wallets; FixedFloat confirmed the theft on 2024-02-18 and, as with its 2024-03-31 repeat, attributed the entry to vulnerabilities in third-party services it depended on rather than to anything it had deployed onchain. Both SlowMist Hacked and DefiLlama classify the event as third-party/infrastructure key leakage. The movement of funds is EOA-to-EOA on the Ethereum leg and UTXO spends on the Bitcoin leg; no smart contract of FixedFloat's was executed, so there is no victim contract to name and no executed EVM code whose age could be measured. I could not obtain a spot-checkable attacker address for this incident from any primary source, and the exclusion does not depend on one: a custodial service compromised through its own infrastructure is outside the cohort whatever the addresses are.

entries.name: Kronos Research exchange API key compromise
entries.reason: OFFCHAIN_ROOT_CAUSE: Kronos Research is a proprietary trading firm. Its own disclosure (2023-11-19) reports unauthorised access to some of its centralised-exchange API keys; SlowMist Hacked records the event as an API-key attack and DefiLlama as 'API Key Compromised'. The roughly 25-26m USD loss was realised inside centralised-exchange accounts through attacker-issued orders and withdrawals, i.e. entirely offchain. No deployed contract was invoked and no protocol invariant failed, so there is no victim contract, no exploit transaction and no executable code whose age could be measured.

entries.name: Resolv TheCounter compromised service key unbacked USR mint
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE and DIRECT_PRIVILEGED_MINT: TheCounter::completeSwap at block 24710031 accepted a 50,000,000 USR output amount from Resolv's long-lived trusted service EOA, then a second call minted 30,000,000 USR. Each call used the compromised service credential to mint directly; neither created persistent state for a later unprivileged exploit. The trace and complete Transfer-from-zero scan isolate these as the only abnormal mints in the window.

entries.name: AFX USDC custody bridge validator hot-key compromise
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: the victim is AFX's own USDC custody bridge on Arbitrum, verified source name 'Bridge', not a proxy, deployed 2026-05-08 by 0xa3eca683bcb9d38102033ca4609eb8f2c960847e; Arbitrum's native bridge was untouched. Decoding the anchor transaction's batchedCreateWithdrawals((address,address,uint64,uint64,(uint256,uint256,uint8)[])[],(uint64,address[],uint64[])) calldata at block 486657995 shows a single withdrawal of 24,150,000,000,000 (24,150,000 USDC at 6 decimals) to 0x2f2974fabc54dba33442261211c06bd20e0feefc, carrying five valid ECDSA signatures against the seven-member hot validator set 0x00bb84af06dac03bfe744da13df9d2d6fd8e77e5, 0x0c95ab7e26df9f63cc6e06df8ee897b822d8c77c, 0x27259f90d6ae500262ace6e8428434e0c1f308f5, 0x2e26de22a92e41704b3ea00cc65a6cda47b12c9e, 0x52d4d9ad78a53a69bd089ee8f282ce0cd0506da7, 0x5553ea7bda594ade7afe91d279779a42b2b84208 and 0xbb472bc3962ad02ac660429fdbb319b5bc66da7b with weights 1428/1429 each, so five stolen keys carried a real quorum. It was released three and a half minutes later by batchedFinalizeWithdrawals(bytes32[]) (tx 0x50d0b3ec6c3f5fce0f10abf81540bbb508f421494aa2b3480c4a264b0436547b, block 486658838, 2026-07-22T21:30:25Z), the same create-then-finalize cadence the bridge uses for ordinary traffic, and the proceeds were bridged to Ethereum by CCTP burns of 7,500,000, 5,895,000 and 5,000,000 USDC. Signature verification executed exactly as written against genuinely authorised keys, so this is validator key compromise and not a defect in the deployed bytecode.

entries.name: Bitrue hot wallet drain
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: Bitrue's own statement of 2023-04-14 reports 'a brief exploit in one of our hot wallets on 07:18 (UTC)' and about 23m USD withdrawn in ETH, QNT, GALA, SHIB, HOT and MATIC from a custodial wallet holding under 5 percent of exchange funds; SlowMist Hacked and DefiLlama both record it as a hot-wallet key compromise. A centralised exchange's custodial wallet is an externally owned account, so there is no victim contract and no protocol invariant to violate. I scanned Ethereum mainnet Transfer logs for QNT 0x4a220e6096b25eadb88358cb44068a3248254675, GALA 0x15d4c048f83bd7e37d49ea4c83a07267ec4203da and MATIC 0x7d1afa7b718fb893db30a3abc0cfc608aacfebb0 across blocks 17043816-17044112 (2023-04-14 06:59:59Z to 08:00Z) and found no bulk movement anywhere near the reported size, so the drained wallet was not an Ethereum mainnet address for those assets and no EVM exploit transaction can be named. The exclusion ground, custodial hot-wallet key compromise per the exchange's own disclosure, does not depend on pinning it.

entries.name: Lykke exchange custodial wallet drain
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: the Swiss exchange Lykke lost about 22.4m USD, roughly 158 BTC and 2,161 ETH plus other assets, on 2024-06-04; the 2024-06-09 candidate date is the date the theft was publicised, not the date it happened. The published sinks are Bitcoin bc1qt64756h9aylujm9tpk826zndegpxtngmr6eqad and Ethereum 0x9172a72f5009ca609833819763a2722e53806443. Spot check: 0x9172a72f5009ca609833819763a2722e53806443 is an externally owned account (code size 0) and its earliest inbound transactions are plain ETH value transfers on 2024-06-04, 189.0165 ETH at 06:48:11Z from 0xc43d1cbacba9dda683a6286a95673c722c0fc488, 1,385.8617 ETH at 06:50:11Z from 0x054e993e0ecc5bf2797515adfc81d58cb8de0478, 300.0141 ETH at 08:05:23Z from 0x1bb2e2d4c782e0a0ea4341f20efdd93b730b1119 and 318.9896 ETH at 08:39:23Z, i.e. several Lykke custodial EOAs emptied in sequence. No contract was called, so no executed EVM code failed and there is no victim contract.

entries.name: Indodax withdrawal system compromise
entries.reason: OFFCHAIN_ROOT_CAUSE: SlowMist's analysis of the Indodax incident explicitly rules out a hot-wallet key compromise and concludes the exchange's withdrawal system itself was hacked, the attacker issuing round-number withdrawals (1 BTC, 3 BTC) with change returned to Indodax-controlled addresses; DefiLlama records the same event as infrastructure key leakage across Ethereum, Polygon and Optimism as well as Bitcoin, for 20-22m USD. Every leg is a custodial exchange wallet, an externally owned account acting on instructions from a compromised offchain withdrawal pipeline. No deployed contract executed defective code, so there is no victim contract and no code-age observation; the exclusion is on offchain infrastructure, which the cohort excludes regardless of chain.

entries.name: IBXtrade Solana presale non-refund
entries.reason: NON_EVM_CHAIN and INSIDER_RUG: the IBXtrade presale ran on Solana, outside the eip155 cohort. The reported 21.8m USD is not an exploit loss at all but unreturned presale deposits: the sale targeted 2,000 SOL and raised over 160,000 SOL with a promise to refund the excess, after which the team ran a cap-raising poll on a site entirely under its own control, declared 65,000 SOL refunded and instead moved that SOL to addresses it had created, with participants reporting no refunds. SlowMist Hacked classifies it as a rug pull. Both grounds are independent: non-EVM chain, and insider action rather than a code defect, with no identifiable victim contract.

entries.name: Bilaxy ERC-20 hot wallet drain
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: Bilaxy's own announcement (2021-08-29) says its ERC-20 hot wallet was hacked and about 295 tokens transferred to 0xa14d5da3c6bf2d9304fe6d4bc6942395b4de048b. Spot check confirms both ends are externally owned accounts with code size 0: 0xa14d5da3c6bf2d9304fe6d4bc6942395b4de048b receives its first token transfers at 2021-08-28T18:19:55Z, all from Bilaxy hot-wallet EOA 0xcce8d59affdd93be338fc77fa0a298c2cb65da59, beginning BIA 563,597,230 (tx 0x243d14ee07ff3578c0...), SPRK 1,570,398, COVA 1,497,243, RECOM 23,805, USDT 414,793, HOGE 1,183,626,188.5, CHAIN 455,867 and JDC 939,140 within the same minute, and continuing through hundreds of listings for the reported 21.7m USD. These are ordinary ERC-20 transfers signed with a stolen key: no contract of the exchange's was executed, so no victim contract and no measurable defective code exist. 2021-08-29 is the disclosure date, one day after the drain.

entries.name: SBI Crypto mining pool wallet drain
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: ZachXBT reported roughly 21m USD of suspicious outflows on 2025-09-24 from wallets belonging to SBI Group's mining subsidiary SBI Crypto, in BTC, ETH, LTC, DOGE and BCH, routed through five instant-exchange services and then into Tornado Cash, with suspected DPRK involvement; CoinDesk carried the report and SlowMist Hacked records it. Four of the five asset legs are on non-eip155 chains and every leg is a custodial mining-pool wallet, i.e. an externally owned account, so no deployed contract executed and no protocol invariant failed. I checked the only publicly labelled EVM address for the entity, Etherscan's 'SBI Crypto Pool' 0x8b4de256180cfec54c436a470af50f9ee2813dbb, and it has no transactions at all in blocks 23422005-23443482 (2025-09-23 to 2025-09-26), so that label is not the drained wallet and no EVM victim contract can be named.

entries.name: BonkDAO BIP-76 governance takeover
entries.reason: NON_EVM_CHAIN and PRIVILEGED_ACTION: BONK and BonkDAO governance run on Solana, outside the eip155 cohort. The attacker bought roughly 4m USD of BONK to acquire sufficient voting power and passed proposal BIP-76, which transferred about 20m USD of BONK out of the treasury to wallets it controlled. SlowMist states explicitly that no smart contract was exploited and the DAO's own voting system was used as designed; DefiLlama classifies it as a governance attack via malicious proposal. Governance executing a proposal it validly approved is a privileged action, not an invariant failure of executed code, so neither ground admits it.

entries.name: Lympo project wallet drain
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: Lympo's statement to its community reports ten project hot wallets compromised and 165.2m LMT, about 18.7m USD, moved and dumped, crashing LMT 92 percent. Spot check on LMT 0x327673ae6b33bd3d90f0096870059994f30dc8af: externally owned account 0xe5e8229c057dcfa804195929293c88c708bd2bb4 (code size 0) received 6,250,000 LMT at 2022-01-10T11:21:09Z from 0x36d97147cf8e1b75254748cf0a102316fcc61697 and 148,600,820 LMT at 12:17:52Z from Lympo wallet 0x526232f70b97938e19394e57bc5ee1d5d929074e (tx 0x5b5e8c2f2c085879c92eb8af0b27f76d7369de04b16a183545e3e54f3e434b53), then sold 154,670,321 LMT into the 0x Protocol ExchangeProxy 0x74de5d4fcbf63e00296fd95d33236b9794016631 at 12:30:03Z (tx 0x4e476c490e5e6c0ce1de8bffeca0121b88a7bb28d272720a294fe2af124d1742). Every step is an ordinary ERC-20 transfer or swap signed with stolen keys; the LMT token and the router both behaved correctly, so there is no defect-bearing victim contract.

entries.name: Rhea Finance NEAR leveraged trading slippage flaw
entries.reason: NON_EVM_CHAIN: Rhea Finance (the merged Ref Finance / Burrow deployment) is a NEAR Protocol application; its lending market and leveraged-trading contracts are Rust/WASM contracts addressed by NEAR named accounts, not eip155 addresses, so the cohort's EVM-only condition excludes it whatever the mechanism. For the record the defect does look like genuine executed code rather than key compromise or configuration: Rhea's 2026-04-18 update attributes about 18.4m USD taken from the reserve pool to the attacker exploiting a vulnerability in the slippage-protection mechanism of the leveraged-trading path, after CertiK's first reading described fake token contracts seeded into new pools to mislead the oracle and validation layers; roughly 3.359m USDC and 1.564m NEAR were returned and 4.34m USDT frozen. Re-enter only if the cohort is ever widened beyond eip155.

entries.name: Ostium OLP vault compromised oracle signer drain
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: the victim is Ostium's public OLP liquidity vault on Arbitrum, TransparentUpgradeableProxy 0x20d419a8e12c45f88fda7c5760bb6923cee27f98 over implementation 0xacff332d0d8c34162be6bbabf7d676fea7cd0f3e (verified name OstiumVault). Scanning native USDC 0xaf88d065e77c8cc2239327c5edb3a432268e5831 Transfer logs across blocks 484136200-484138604 shows the vault paying attacker 0x321df194646029e7a6193ea05573d4b9c398bfd9 in six settlements: 6,290,901.90 + 4,763,111.22 + 718,959.42 USDC in the anchor transaction at block 484137113 (2026-07-15T14:18:48Z), then 4,493,501.10 (0xd9f91cc3eaec695f45bffad3a068fa52e1625ed44bfcc47d6ac3938f78d9061d), 3,594,800.70 (0x3b04639ab9b40760b2138e7bfa7eccc9657f3a767a5c414dbb1b3632ed71f3bf), 2,696,100.30 (0x6c254483fa47a14622662e792bc3728ab3c408a33d3cbb5712434ba96f5ecdc2) and 1,078,439.58 (0xfaf6d3d4d7f1a75bfc11fb4d36d0525791546267fda1cdd371703ce03ae8ba8c), about 23.6m USDC in total, all batched through attacker contract 0xfe12f6360000de49d5506d52ee5ac4bc9dd5bd2e from EOA 0xd1794196f0fc99c7f27970e661597d77d9a85869. The window matches founder Kaledora Fontana's statement that funds left the public OLP vault between 14:18 and 14:23 UTC. SlowMist and DefiLlama both attribute the exploit to a compromised oracle signer key used to submit fraudulent future-dated price reports, which the settlement path then honoured; without that key the attacker's trades do not settle profitably, so the stolen signer is the necessary cause. Reviewer flag: if a full post-mortem later shows the vault would also have accepted stale or future-dated reports from an honest signer, the acceptance logic becomes an independent code defect and this lead should be reopened.

entries.name: Grinex exchange hot wallet drain
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: Grinex, the Kyrgyzstan-registered exchange that absorbed the sanctioned Garantex's liquidity and users, suspended trading and withdrawals after a hot-wallet infrastructure breach. Elliptic puts the theft at about 15m USD of USDT taken from Grinex-associated wallets and routed through TRON and Ethereum, then converted into TRX and ETH to reduce the chance of a Tether freeze; the exchange's own notice claims over 1bn rubles, about 13.1m USD. TRON is not an eip155 chain, and the Ethereum leg consists of ERC-20 transfers out of custodial externally owned accounts, so no deployed contract executed defective code and there is no victim contract to name.

entries.name: Rain exchange custodial wallet drain
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: about 14.8m USD was taken from the custodial wallets of Rain, the Bahrain-licensed exchange, across Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP and Solana on 2024-04-29; DefiLlama classifies the event as a private-key compromise and the public reporting attributes it to DPRK-linked actors, with no protocol or contract exploit alleged by any source. Three of the four asset legs are on non-eip155 chains and all four are exchange custody addresses, i.e. externally owned accounts moved with stolen keys, so there is no victim contract, no exploit transaction against deployed code and nothing whose code age could be measured. SlowMist Hacked carries no entry for this incident and I could not obtain a spot-checkable address for any leg; the exclusion ground does not depend on one.

entries.name: SQTokenStaking hardcoded backdoor beneficiary
entries.reason: INSIDER_RUG: the deployed Staking contract carries a hardcoded backdoor beneficiary, so no invariant of the code failed and there is nothing to age. The legacy summary that transferOwnership had no access control is wrong - transferOwnership is onlyOwner, but the deployed Ownable._checkOwner() reads: if (owner() != _msgSender() && _msgSender() != 0xe746c9043aa0106853c5e4380a9a307fe385378e) revert, with that address literal compiled into the runtime (one occurrence in the 24,462-byte runtime at block 97836947). Proved by simulation at block 97836947, where owner() is 0x..dEaD: transferOwnership succeeds from 0xe746c904.. and reverts both from project operator 0x1df1d1e2.. and from an unrelated address. The same literal appears in sibling contracts IConf 0x08f7fd1b.. and PotatoCoin 0x84791ba6.., all deployed in one batch on 2026-01-29 funded by operator 0x1df1d1e2.., and the backdoor EOA was funded 41 days before the victim contract existed (block 72147100). Exploiting it requires being that specific address, so this is author-installed authority rather than a defect any caller could trigger. The PoC asserts 346,137.034345014454603094 USDT, but the incident yields no code-age observation.
