entries.name: WOO X exchange developer-environment phishing drain
entries.reason: OFFCHAIN_ROOT_CAUSE and KEY_COMPROMISE: DefiLlama's hack registry (api.llama.fi/hacks) records this as classification 'Social Engineering', technique 'Phishing', targetType 'CEX', 14.0m USD, spread across Bitcoin, Ethereum, Arbitrum and BSC. The compromised asset was WOO X's own developer environment; the attacker then signed ordinary withdrawals out of exchange-custody wallets. One of the four asset legs (Bitcoin) is not an eip155 chain, and on the EVM legs an exchange hot wallet is an externally owned account: no contract of WOO X's executed, no protocol invariant was violated, and there is no deployed code whose age could be measured. WOO X published no contract address or exploit transaction and I could not obtain a spot-checkable custody address for any leg; the exclusion ground does not depend on one, because a phished developer credential is outside the cohort whichever address was drained.

entries.name: M2 exchange hot wallet drain
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: DefiLlama records classification 'Key Compromise', technique 'Hot Wallet Key Compromised', targetType 'CEX', 13.7m USD taken from the Abu Dhabi exchange M2 across Ethereum, Solana and Bitcoin. Two of the three legs (Solana, Bitcoin) are outside eip155, and the Ethereum leg is ERC-20 and ether transfers signed out of custodial externally owned accounts. M2 operates no deployed protocol contract on any chain, so there is no victim contract, no exploit transaction against deployed code, and no code state whose age could be measured. M2 covered the loss from its own reserves the same week; that does not create a contract-level defect.

entries.name: flash.sx / vaults.sx EOS reentrancy drain
entries.reason: NON_EVM_CHAIN: DefiLlama places the incident on EOS and records the defective code's language as C++. EOSIO contracts are C++ compiled to WASM and are addressed by 12-character account names, not by eip155 addresses, so there is no address, no runtime bytecode and no codeHash the verifier could resolve. The mechanism itself does look like a genuine executed-code defect rather than a key compromise: flash.sx was an EOSIO flash-loan primitive and vaults.sx the yield vault backing it, and the attacker re-entered the vault from inside the flash-loan callback for about 13m USD. The cohort is eip155-only, so it is excluded on chain grounds regardless. Re-enter only if the cohort is ever widened beyond eip155.

entries.name: GDAC exchange hot wallet drain
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: DefiLlama records classification 'Key Compromise', technique 'Hot Wallet Key Compromised', targetType 'CEX', 13.9m USD, with no chain attribution at all because the drained assets were custodial balances rather than protocol positions: about 61 BTC, 350.5 ETH, 10,000,000 WEMIX and 220,000 USDT, roughly a quarter of the Korean exchange GDAC's total custody. The BTC leg is not an eip155 chain and the remaining legs are ordinary transfers signed out of exchange-owned externally owned accounts, so no deployed contract of GDAC's executed and no invariant of any contract was violated. Dates differ across sources: DefiLlama records 2023-04-08, the incident occurred on 2023-04-09 KST, and the web lead's 2023-04-10 is the public announcement.

entries.name: pNetwork pBTC bridge forged-event drain (September 2021)
entries.reason: OFFCHAIN_ROOT_CAUSE: the loss was 277 BTC, about 12.7m USD, released from pNetwork's Bitcoin-side vault. DefiLlama records the event as 'Bridge & Cross-Chain' / 'Spoofed Event Log' over chains BSC and Bitcoin, and names the defective code's language as Rust: the pTokens bridge core that decides whether a redeem happened is Rust software running off-chain, not EVM bytecode. I verified onchain that the BSC side lost nothing. The pBTC token 0xed28a457a5a76596ac48d87c0f577020f6ea1c4c (AdminUpgradeabilityProxy over implementation 0xd61372d1c3e0a0925467317425359fb2959fe186) has zero Transfer events from the zero address in blocks 11035530 (2021-09-18T23:59:58Z) through 11092771 (2021-09-21), i.e. no unbacked mint, and the largest single pBTC movement in that whole window is 51.7499 pBTC at block 11067993 (tx 0x2876012ade42384bd6a5abe3326f4fa1c02b13c7121e8333b49216b8d9e3e88e), nowhere near 277. So there is no EVM victim contract: the depleted asset is native BTC on a non-eip155 chain and the failure is an off-chain validator honouring a log it did not authenticate, the same shape as the already-excluded THORChain Bifrost incidents.

entries.name: Ionic Protocol fake LBTC collateral listing
entries.reason: CAUSAL_CONFIGURATION_WITH_OFFCHAIN_TRIGGER: Ionic's deployer created ionLBTC in transaction 0x0b867a1dfd937981202cef46d533bbf66b4f737ba38a37d7fc633647e96d4e6d with attacker-controlled token 0x964dd444e3192f636322229080a576077b06fba3 as underlying collateral. After 250 fake LBTC was minted, later permissionless supplies and borrows depleted real assets. Reopened because social engineering caused a persistent listing later exercised by ordinary callers; review must anchor every listing and risk write and reconcile the 8.6 million versus 12.3 million USD loss reports.

entries.name: Triple-A payments hot wallet drain
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: DefiLlama records classification 'Key Compromise', technique 'Hot Wallet Key Compromised', targetType 'Payments', 9.7m USD (the web lead's 11.8m is the higher press figure), across Ethereum, Tron and Arbitrum. Triple-A is a licensed payment processor holding client crypto in company custody; the drained balances are custodial externally owned accounts, and the Tron leg is not an eip155 chain. No Triple-A protocol contract exists to be the victim, no deployed code was executed outside its specification, and no code state can be aged. The company's own disclosure attributes the loss to unauthorised access to company wallets, not to any contract.

entries.name: BitoPro exchange hot wallet drain
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE and OFFCHAIN_ROOT_CAUSE: DefiLlama records classification 'Frontend & Infrastructure', technique 'Key Leaked via Infrastructure', targetType 'CEX', 11.5m USD, across Ethereum, Tron, Solana and Polygon. The Taiwanese exchange BitoPro's own disclosure and the subsequent DPRK attribution describe malware planted during a hot-wallet system migration that exfiltrated signing material from the exchange's own servers; the outbound movements are then ordinary transfers from custodial externally owned accounts. Two of the four legs (Tron, Solana) are outside eip155 and none of the four involves a BitoPro-deployed contract, so there is no victim contract and no defective executed code to age.

entries.name: UXLINK Safe owner takeover and unauthorised mint
entries.reason: CAUSAL_CONFIGURATION_WITH_OFFCHAIN_TRIGGER: threshold-authorized Safe transactions added attacker owner 0x2ef43c1d0c88c071d242b6c2d0430e1751607b87, removed the three prior owners, and set threshold 1. The next day that persistent owner state authorized six UXLINK mints. Reopened because the owner takeover created a condition exercised by later transactions even though social engineering supplied the original signatures; review must anchor the final owner change and measure actual victim depletion rather than nominal mint value.

entries.name: Garden Finance solver key leak
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE and OFFCHAIN_ROOT_CAUSE: DefiLlama records classification 'Frontend & Infrastructure', technique 'Key Leaked via Infrastructure', 11.4m USD, across Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base and Solana. Garden is an intent-based cross-chain swap protocol whose solvers hold their own inventory and sign fills; the compromise was of a solver's operational infrastructure, so the attacker moved solver-owned capital with a stolen key rather than defeating any invariant of Garden's HTLC contracts. The Solana leg is outside eip155. This is a different event from the 2026-07-26 Garden database breach (450k USD), which DefiLlama lists separately. No Garden contract was drained by an attacker without the solver's key, so there is no defect-bearing victim contract; if a later postmortem shows the settlement contracts released escrowed user funds on a signature they should have rejected, the lead should be reopened.

entries.name: Blend Pools V2 oracle manipulation
entries.reason: NON_EVM_CHAIN: DefiLlama records Blend Pools V2 on Stellar, 10.97m USD, classification 'Oracle Manipulation', technique 'Spot Price Manipulation'. Blend is a Soroban lending protocol; its pools are Rust/WASM contracts addressed by Stellar strkeys (C... contract IDs), not eip155 addresses, so no address, runtime bytecode or codeHash exists that this dataset could measure. The cohort is eip155-only, so the incident is excluded on chain grounds whatever the mechanism. Re-enter only if the cohort is ever widened beyond eip155.

entries.name: Dego Finance minter key compromise
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE and PRIVILEGED_ACTION: DefiLlama records classification 'Key Compromise', technique 'Deployer Key Compromised', 10m USD across Ethereum, BSC and Cronos. Verified onchain: the only mint of the DEGO token 0x88ef27e69108b2633f8e1c184cc37940a075cc02 in blocks 14174988-14187946 (2022-02-10 to 2022-02-11) is 953,590.33 DEGO to 0xd2b2755a4bdcaf415e9a74e3efe41d23d2f70c53 at 2022-02-10T00:56:12Z, block 14175251, in tx 0x4195bf8ad88ee40a3df2d851820d4d35a8bde498a2b369040f71aaf1c1b23251. That transaction is a direct call of mint(address,uint256) (selector 0x40c10f19, 138-byte calldata) from externally owned account 0x20fe4b1ed95911487499e53355bb8f14a881d735 straight to the token, with no intermediate contract and no defeated check: the caller simply held the token's minter authority. The BSC-side DEGO 0x3fda9383a84c05ec8f7630fe10adf1fd13c5c79b has zero mints in the corresponding window (blocks 15118825-15176352). A privileged mint executed by whoever holds the minter key is the correct behaviour of the deployed code, so there is no invariant failure to age.

entries.name: Wanchain Cardano bridge signature verification flaw
entries.reason: NON_EVM_CHAIN: DefiLlama records the incident on Cardano only, 10m USD, classification 'Input Validation', technique 'Signature Verification Flaw', bridgeHack true, targetType 'Chain', and names the defective code's language as Haskell. Wanchain's Cardano-side bridge logic is a Plutus validator written in Plutus Tx / Haskell and addressed by a Cardano script address, so there is neither an eip155 address nor EVM runtime bytecode whose age this dataset could measure, and the depleted vault is on Cardano rather than on the BNB Chain leg the web lead names. The cohort is eip155-only. Re-enter only if a postmortem shows the released value actually came out of a Wanchain contract deployed on BNB Chain or another eip155 chain, which would move the victim onto an EVM chain.

entries.name: MyAlgo wallet CDN compromise
entries.reason: NON_EVM_CHAIN and OFFCHAIN_ROOT_CAUSE: DefiLlama records MyAlgo on Algorand, 9.2m USD, classification 'Frontend & Infrastructure', technique 'CDN Compromise', targetType 'Wallet', language JavaScript. Algorand is not an eip155 chain, and the defective artefact was the wallet's browser JavaScript, served from a compromised CDN, which exfiltrated users' mnemonics; the subsequent transfers were valid Algorand payments signed with the stolen seeds. Both grounds bite independently: there is no EVM chain involved and no deployed contract executed any defective code, only client-side script outside any chain's state.

entries.name: Astra Nova managed-account key compromise
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: DefiLlama records classification 'Key Compromise', technique 'Private Key Compromised', targetType 'AI Agent', 9.09m USD on Ethereum; the web lead agrees the compromised party was a third-party managed account rather than Astra Nova's own contracts. I checked the project's RVV token 0x80563fc2dd549bf36f82d3bf3b970bb5b08dbddb on BSC across blocks 65108334-65223513 (2025-10-19 to 2025-10-20): zero mints from the zero address and no single transfer at or above 10,000,000 RVV, so the token contract neither over-issued nor was drained and is not the victim. The loss is stolen-key movement of balances held in an externally owned or custodially managed account, with no deployed contract executing outside its specification and nothing whose code age could be measured.

entries.name: Holograph operator hardcoded messaging-caller backdoor
entries.reason: INSIDER_RUG and ATTACKER_DEPLOYED: the Mantle mint did not use the lzReceive weakness at all, it used a hardcoded address literal planted in Holographs own operator bytecode. getJobDetails at block 65068617 shows the job was planted at block 63225816 on 2024-05-01, 43 days earlier, by 0x92d1f6fe..3d79: attacker EOA 0xc0ffee78121f208475abdd2cf0853a7afed64749 called adminCall(address,bytes) on 0x777c19834a1a2ff6353a1e9cfb7c799ed7943a11 which called operator.crossChainMessage. Four such plants exist. The operator implementation active then, 0x34b2521f33f224bf21b7f5a8e17354e90c59d453 (byte-identical on Mantle and Ethereum, runtime hash 0xa7a3b24b..1d5c), contains verbatim: require(msg.sender == address(_messagingModule()) || msg.sender == 0x777c19834a1a2ff6353a1e9cfb7c799ed7943a11), and _messagingModuleSlot held the canonical 0x7969414a..0271 throughout, so only the literal branch let the call through. 0x777c1983.. was created by 0xc0ffee78 through the attackers own CREATE2 factory 0x0c8af56f76.. on 2023-08-04, five months before the backdoored implementation existed; its getAdmin() is 0xc0ffee78 and its implementation slot points to unverified custom bytecode differing per chain, unlike Holographs canonical verified LayerZeroModule 0x7d4807de... Triggering it requires being that address, whose only entry is admin-gated adminCall, so the settled backdoor convention makes this author-or-attacker-installed authority rather than a defect any caller could trigger. The Ethereum leg 0x0cc143cc..46396 is downstream and yields nothing: its job hash 0x3f9c5cc1..6571 matches the last Mantle bridge-out 0x845dafda..6449 exactly, so Ethereum minted the legitimate counterpart of a real Mantle burn. All 10e9 HLG minted on Mantle was burned out in seven transactions and no other Mantle HLG mint exists in the tokens history. The lzReceive weakness described in reporting is real as code, only caller() == _lZEndpointSlot and _srcAddress[0:20] == address() are enforced, but no leg of this campaign on chains 1 or 5000 used it.

entries.name: Crema Finance CLMM tick-account substitution
entries.reason: NON_EVM_CHAIN: Crema Finance is a concentrated-liquidity AMM deployed as a Solana BPF program written in Rust, and the whole campaign (flash loan from Solend, a self-created account passed where the pool's real tick account was expected, forged fee data, then claim) executed inside that Solana program. DefiLlama's hack registry records chain 'Solana', language 'Rust', classification 'Access Control', technique 'Improper Access Control', 8,800,000 USD, dated 2022-07-02. Solana has no eip155 chain id, emits no EVM bytecode and has no address whose runtime code could be hashed or aged, so cohort condition 1 (a defect in executed EVM code) cannot be satisfied. No Ethereum-side or other eip155 leg of this incident exists.

entries.name: ALEX Protocol self-listing verification flaw
entries.reason: NON_EVM_CHAIN: ALEX is a DEX/launchpad on Stacks and its contracts are written in Clarity, not Solidity, running on the Stacks (Clarity VM) chain. DefiLlama records chain 'Stacks', language 'Clarity', classification 'Access Control', technique 'Caller Impersonation', 8,373,000 USD, dated 2025-06-06; the self-listing path failed to verify that the caller matched the token being listed. Stacks is not an eip155 chain, has no EVM runtime and no code hash that the verifier could pin, so the incident yields no code-age observation for this dataset. ALEX's earlier 2024-05-16 loss (4.3m, phishing) is likewise out of scope.

entries.name: Haven Protocol xUSD offshore mint-validation flaws
entries.reason: NON_EVM_CHAIN: Haven Protocol is a standalone CryptoNote/Monero fork with its own C++ daemon and ring-signature ledger; the 2021 exploit series minted unbacked xUSD/xAsset supply by abusing the offshore conversion and mint-validation logic in that daemon. DefiLlama records chain 'Haven', classification 'Token & Share Accounting', technique 'Infinite Mint', 8,187,000 USD, dated 2021-07-03, with language null (no Solidity involved). There is no eip155 chain, no contract address and no EVM transaction anywhere in the causal path, so cohort conditions 1 and 2 both fail.

entries.name: Slope mobile wallet seed-phrase logging
entries.reason: OFFCHAIN_INFRASTRUCTURE: the Slope mobile wallet transmitted users' mnemonic seed phrases in clear text to Slope's centralised Sentry logging service, and whoever obtained that log signed ordinary transfers out of roughly nine thousand Solana accounts. DefiLlama records chain 'Solana', classification 'Frontend & Infrastructure', technique 'Key Stored Publicly', targetType 'Wallet', 4,100,000 USD, dated 2022-08-02 (the web lead's ~8m is the upper press estimate). The defect is in an off-chain mobile client, the victims are externally owned Solana accounts, and Solana is not an eip155 chain: no deployed EVM code failed an invariant and there is no victim contract to age.

entries.name: BitKeep trojanised Android APK distribution
entries.reason: OFFCHAIN_INFRASTRUCTURE: attackers repackaged BitKeep's Android wallet (v7.2.9) with code that exfiltrated users' private keys and distributed it through unofficial download mirrors; the resulting drains are ordinary ERC-20/BEP-20 transfer and native-value transactions signed out of the victims' own externally owned accounts on BNB Chain, Ethereum, Polygon and Tron. The compromised artefact is a Java/Kotlin APK, not deployed EVM bytecode, and no contract in the causal path failed any invariant - the token contracts executed correctly for a caller holding the keys. There is therefore no victim contract and no defect-bearing code state to age. Compromised credentials and off-chain client behaviour are both excluded by METHODOLOGY.

entries.name: Bittensor malicious PyPI package coldkey exfiltration
entries.reason: NON_EVM_CHAIN: a malicious release of the `bittensor` Python package on PyPI exfiltrated users' unencrypted coldkeys, and the attacker then signed ordinary balance transfers on the Bittensor (Subtensor) Substrate chain. DefiLlama records language 'Python', classification 'Social Engineering', technique 'Malware', 8,000,000 USD, dated 2024-07-02, with an empty chain list. Bittensor is an SS58 Substrate network with no eip155 chain id and no EVM contract state at the time of the incident, and the defect lives in an off-chain Python dependency. Both cohort condition 1 (executed EVM code) and condition 2 (an eip155 anchor) fail.

entries.name: Trust Wallet browser extension 2.68 malicious release
entries.reason: OFFCHAIN_INFRASTRUCTURE: the loss originates in a poisoned build of the Trust Wallet browser extension (version 2.68), i.e. in JavaScript shipped to users' browsers, not in any deployed contract. DefiLlama records classification 'Frontend & Infrastructure', technique 'Supply Chain Attack', targetType 'Wallet', chains 'Ethereum, Bitcoin, Solana', language null, 8,500,000 USD, dated 2025-12-25. The drains are ordinary transfers and approvals signed with keys the extension handed to the attacker, spread across chains two of which (Bitcoin, Solana) are not eip155 at all; the ERC-20 contracts touched on the Ethereum leg behaved exactly as written. No deployed EVM code violated an invariant, so there is no victim contract and no code age to measure.

entries.name: Zapper frontend DNS hijack and drainer approvals
entries.reason: OFFCHAIN_INFRASTRUCTURE: Zapper's domain was hijacked at the DNS layer and visitors were served a wallet-drainer page that asked them to sign ordinary ERC-20 approvals and Permit2 signatures; the subsequent transferFrom calls executed exactly as the token contracts specify. DefiLlama records classification 'Frontend & Infrastructure', technique 'DNS Hijack', chains 'Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon, Base', dated 2025-04-01, and notably records amount null - the 7.9m figure in the lead is an unsourced press estimate with no per-victim accounting. The victims are individual externally owned accounts, Zapper's own deployed contracts were not implicated, and no EVM code failed an invariant, so the incident yields neither a victim contract nor a measurable code state.

entries.name: ODIN.FUN bonding-curve price manipulation
entries.reason: NON_EVM_CHAIN: ODIN.FUN is a token launchpad running as an Internet Computer canister written in Motoko; the attacker manipulated the bonding-curve spot price inside that canister to extract roughly 7m USD of BTC-denominated liquidity. DefiLlama records chain 'ICP', language 'Motoko', classification 'Oracle Manipulation', technique 'Spot Price Manipulation', 7,000,000 USD, dated 2025-08-12. The Internet Computer executes WebAssembly canisters, has no eip155 chain id, no EVM bytecode and no address whose runtime hash could be pinned, so no code-age observation is possible.

entries.name: Yala YU deployer-key unauthorised mint
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: the attacker obtained a Yala deployment key and used the mint authority it carried to issue unbacked YU, then swapped the proceeds into roughly 7.64m USDC. DefiLlama records classification 'Key Compromise', technique 'Deployer Key Compromised', targetType 'Token', language 'Rust', chains 'Solana, Ethereum', 7,640,000 USD, dated 2025-09-14. The mint executed through the authority the deployed program grants its own key holder, so no invariant of any deployed code was violated; the primary leg is a Solana (Rust) program outside eip155, and the Ethereum leg is ordinary token movement. Compromised credentials and privileged actions are excluded by METHODOLOGY, so this yields no code-age row.

entries.name: HTX hot wallet drain (September 2023)
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: roughly 5,000 ETH (about 8m USD) left an HTX custodial hot wallet on 2023-09-24/25 as ordinary value transfers; HTX operates no deployed protocol contract that could have been exploited, and the attacker returned the funds on 2023-10-07 in exchange for a 250 ETH bounty that Justin Sun publicly confirmed - behaviour consistent with key theft, not with an exploited contract. DefiLlama records classification 'Key Compromise', technique 'Hot Wallet Key Compromised', targetType 'CEX', chain 'Ethereum', 8,000,000 USD, dated 2023-09-25. This is a distinct event from the 2023-11-22 HTX and HECO Bridge operator-key compromise already excluded in this file. With only externally owned custodial accounts in the causal path there is no victim contract, no exploit transaction against deployed code and no code state whose age could be measured.

entries.name: Zoth USD0PPSubVault deployer-key malicious upgrade
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: Zoth's deployer key held the UUPS upgrade authority on the USD0PPSubVaultUpgradeable proxy 0x82f3a0392f58c50fa90542519832471bae93e43e, and whoever obtained it called upgradeToAndCall() in transaction 0xb2335f7bf58abbcaa006d0a2bed7db2c64a5dabed56fb1759260adc012c49abe at block 22094140 to install a self-authored implementation 0xc89d7894341e13d5067d003af5346b257d861f56 carrying an unrestricted withdraw(), then emptied the vault 36 seconds later in 0x33bf669d125d11c432ac9b52b9d56161101c072fd8b0ac2aa390f5760fb50ca4. The proxy was created by Zoth deployer 0x3604582f56565d7060d73829ffb9ebd579218dca, not by the attack sender 0x3b33c5cd948be5863b72cb3d6e9c0b36e67d01e5, and this was the seventh Upgraded event on the proxy. No pre-existing Zoth code failed an invariant: the upgrade mechanism executed exactly as designed for the holder of the upgrade key, and the only 'defective' artifact is the attacker's own implementation, whose 36-second mechanical age measures the attacker's deployment rather than any battle-tested code. DefiLlama also classifies it 'Key Compromise / Private Key Compromised'. This matches legacy row protocols/zoth.json#0, which was already held out of the primary dataset for the same reason.

entries.name: THORChain Asgard vault GG20 threshold-signature key reconstruction
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: THORChain's published post-mortem attributes the 2026-05-15 loss of about 10.7m USD across Bitcoin, Ethereum, Base and BNB Chain to a vulnerability in the GG20 threshold-ECDSA implementation used by THORNode: a malicious node operator progressively leaked key material until it could reconstruct the complete private key of one Asgard vault. That signing stack is off-chain Go code, and DefiLlama's registry records language null and targetType 'Chain' for this row (contrast the two 2021 THORChain rows, which it labels Solidity). Once the vault key was held, the Ethereum-side Router 0xd37bbe5744d730a1d98d8dc97c42f0ca46ad7146 simply honoured transferOut calls from the vault address as its source specifies; an onchain review of every Router transaction in blocks 25096819-25111182 (2026-05-15T00:00Z to 2026-05-17T00:00Z) shows only routine transferOut and depositWithExpiry traffic from Asgard vault accounts, with no anomalous entry point, no upgrade and no failed authorisation check. A cryptographic flaw in an off-chain MPC library is not a defect in executed EVM code, and two of the four affected chains (Bitcoin, and THORChain's own Cosmos-SDK L1) are not eip155 at all.

entries.name: DAO Maker SHO deposit contract admin-role drain (August 2021)
entries.reason: PRIVILEGED_ACTION: DAO Maker's own statement of 2021-08-12 says the company 'faced malicious use of one of our wallets with access to admin privileges', and the chain agrees. The sender 0x0eba461d9829c4e464a68d4857350476cfb6f559 had been operating DAO Maker admin functions since April 2021 (changeAssetDepositState on the SHO deposit contract 0x41b856701bb8c24cece2af10651bfafebb57cf49 on 2021-04-12 and 2021-04-21, addOrganizer/removeOrganizer/changeOrganizerAddress on 0x380c2c68ebcb38473e91b32e19ffb5519d7822b7 through 2021-08-03). At 2021-08-12T01:17:13Z it deployed the helper contract 0x1c93290202424902a5e708b95f4ba23a3f2f3cee (verified source, contract 'XXX', hardcoding victim 0x41b856..., collector 0xd8428836ed2a36bd67cd5b157b50813b30208f50 and USDC), then at 01:20:53Z and 01:27:39Z called grantRole(bytes32,address) on the victim to authorise it. The helper loops over user addresses calling selector 0x4b4f892a getUserAvailableBalance(address,address) and then 0x50b158e4 withdrawFromUser(address,address,uint256) - a role-gated administrative function that executed exactly as written for a caller holding the role. The first successful drain is 0x26aa86261c834e837f6be93b2d589724ed5ae644bc8f4b8af2207e6bd70828f9 at block 13007501 index 7, status 1 (an earlier attempt at 01:24:48Z, 0x11671333..., reverted before the second grantRole); about thirty further successful h(address[]) calls follow through 2021-08-12T18:18:02Z from 0xd8428836..., 0xed3112d1cf4895eb15f52e71f492235ed8ca7897, 0x414354db069cea6fa536c3d2ea1bbf5730b7715c and others. eth_getLogs over USDC and USDT for blocks 13006975-13008611 shows 0x41b856... emitting 5,252 outbound USDC transfers totalling 7,387,245 USDC in that window, matching DAO Maker's '5251 users affected, approximately 7m'. This is the August incident and is distinct from the already-admitted September 2021 record incidents/1/0xd5e2edd6089dcf5dca78c0ccbdf659acedab173a8ab3cb65720e35b640c0af7c.json (unprotected init() on the vesting minimal proxies). No deployed-code invariant failed here: an authorised administrative withdrawal path was used by whoever controlled the admin key.

entries.name: Anyswap V3 router MPC key recovery from ECDSA nonce reuse
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: the Anyswap V3 loss came from the attacker recovering the router's MPC private key, not from any contract flaw. Two transactions signed by the V3 MPC account reused the same ECDSA nonce (identical r value), which makes the secret key recoverable by elementary algebra; the signing stack is Anyswap's off-chain Go MPC node, and the router's Solidity simply honours calls from `mpc()`. The onchain response confirms the diagnosis: on the Ethereum AnyswapV4Router 0x6b7a87899490ece95443e979ca9485cbe7e71522 the MPC was rotated away from 0x8b44a687224496276811555efa3f2d0acd667a72 the day after the incident, in transaction 0x65651a6ba929fcb12ddcacd9a92fc131e1893dd0d0787f3c7cc787e4dad91ec6 (changeMPC(address), block 12806663, 2021-07-11T14:56:16Z, sent by the compromised MPC itself), with storage slot 0 (_oldMPC) becoming 0x8b44a687... and slot 1 (_newMPC) becoming 0x2a038e100f8b85df21e4d44121bdbfe0c288a869; nothing about the deployed code changed. This incident is distinct from the January 2022 AnyswapV4Router permit flaw already admitted as incidents/1/0xe50ed602bd916fc304d53c4fed236698b71691a95774ff0aeeb74b699c6227f7.json, which is a genuine code defect. Compromised credentials are excluded by METHODOLOGY, and a nonce-reuse bug in an off-chain signer is not executed EVM code.

entries.name: GAMEE GMEE deployer-key recoverERC721s drain
entries.reason: KEY_COMPROMISE: Halborn's analysis and GAMEE's own disclosure attribute the loss to unauthorised access to an outdated GitLab repository that contained the project deployer's private key. Onchain, the compromised owner 0x566b788de3969d35711f6a0fc543b00ed7260cdc called the owner-only rescue function recoverERC721s (selector 0xc3666c36) on the verified PolygonGMEE token 0xcf32822ff397ef82425153a9dcb726e5ff61dca7 twice, at 2024-01-22T18:31:15Z (block 52629016, moving 299,999,999 GMEE to 0x16afa519642c932b073cd21d82162bdc7a471b86) and again at 20:31:03Z, then called transferOwnership on the same token at 22:35:32Z and on roughly fifteen further GAMEE contracts between 2024-01-23T03:10Z and 04:02Z. The PolygonGMEE source exposes recoverERC20s/recoverERC721s behind a _requireOwnership guard that executed exactly as written for the legitimate owner address, so no deployed-code invariant was violated; the defect is credential storage in an off-chain repository. Total press figure roughly 600m GMEE, about 7m USD.

entries.name: SOMESING SSX project wallet drain
entries.reason: NO_VICTIM_CONTRACT: the stolen SSX came out of externally owned wallets, and no token was minted. SOMESING Exchange (SSX) is a KIP-7/ERC-20 on Kaia (formerly Klaytn, eip155:8217) at 0xdcd62c57182e780e23d2313c4782709da85b9d6c, 18 decimals; eth_call totalSupply() returns exactly 5,054,571,320 SSX at the block for 2024-01-20T00:00Z, at latest, and at the block for 2024-02-03T00:00Z, so DefiLlama's 'Unbacked Mint' classification for this row is wrong (its 'Ethereum' chain and 'Solidity' language fields are wrong too - the SSG token 0x63dec0c0cf911d8967446ce422dd31f13e1e0556 that CoinGecko now lists did not yet exist on 2024-01-27, eth_getCode at Kaia block 144333904 returns 0x). Scanning every SSX Transfer log over Kaia blocks 144161104-144420304 (2024-01-25T00:00Z to 2024-01-28T00:00Z), plus a wider sweep of blocks 143642704-145025104 (2024-01-19 to 2024-02-04) that found no SSX transfer above 80,000,000 tokens other than the two below, shows the loss as two ordinary transfers out of funded EOAs: 162,047,818 SSX at 2024-01-26T16:18:02Z (block 144306186, tx 0x72e79da7d163c2b8ac55e0072f206dc073a11a488644f6e93276d4213c763544) from 0x3c2bcee93ad378e5f12fa4170d9d8a0707831d69 (balance 167,047,818 SSX immediately before) to 0x43edf0fdeaa30d3af23b0bb005d10833d8603ae4, and 210,446,564 SSX at 2024-01-26T20:18:21Z (block 144320605, tx 0xaaef0b8113d5ad48009a4df3ffb64b653007fb8547b09a9acae9b7850dac786e) from 0x0b7da3649ede697993c847c8169700bd911ebd57 to 0x1dc9223a74c088117772e769f9769911d4c95985, both followed within the hour by 3m-64m SSX tranches routed through 0x4c973076cc379af726d1cf4aaf0f952f77265bee into Kaia DEX pools. eth_getCode returns 0x for all four of those addresses, so every party in the causal path is an EOA and the only contract touched is the SSX token itself, which executed transfer() correctly. A wallet drain with no defective contract yields no code-age observation.
